facts.text: We make burkinis and modest swim sets as two-piece or three-piece outfits. Each one pairs a long-sleeve tunic or a swim dress with full-length leggings and is finished with a hood or a separate hijab. Our swim dresses are cut to be layered over the leggings. If you would rather offer a single garment, we also produce full-coverage one-piece swimsuits and integrated body suits with the leg coverage built in.

Alongside our sets, we produce swim hijabs and caps, full-coverage one-piece swimsuits, rash guards with long sleeves and swim leggings for surfing and other water sports, beach and poolside cover-ups, kaftans and robes in fast-drying cloth, and modest swimwear for kids.
For modest swimmers who train, we manufacture custom sport burkini sets. We also offer two-tone panel constructions with a sportswear look.

Our wholesale stock includes a selection of modest swimwear and burkini styles. We also have ready-made designs cut on patterns we already use, such as two-piece and three-piece sets that pair a tunic with leggings, so you can buy without developing a new style. Ask us for our latest Modest Swimwear and Burkinis line sheet to see what we have now. Sizing, colour and shade may differ from one item to the next. You can add your own labels and branding to our ready-made burkini designs without any new development. The design itself stays in our range and is open to every buyer, but the prints, artwork and branding you supply are kept for you alone.

We print the tunic, leggings and hijab of one set in the same run, using sublimation on polyester or digital pigment printing on nylon, so the colour stays consistent across all three pieces. Where the print crosses a side seam or shoulder join, we line the motif up when laying out and cutting the pattern pieces.

For custom prints we offer sublimation on polyester fabrics and digital pigment printing on nylon fabrics, as either all-over or placement designs, and embroidery is available as an extra decoration. Send your artwork in AI or PDF format and we print it photo-sharp, with results that hold up for over 200 hours in chlorinated and salt water.
Both OEM and ODM work is possible: a new style can start from your own design, a picture or just an idea.

Our private label service covers custom branding, tags and packaging. We make customised tags and packaging to fit your budget, and we quote for your company name and logo on packaging according to the packaging you choose.
We manufacture swimwear ourselves in a single factory of our own in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.
Production and export sit in one company that owns its factory, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.
Quality is checked at every stage of an order: fabric on arrival, cutting, sewing, then random checks and a full final inspection.
Our production holds OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.
Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, a level set so that small and growing labels can order.
A first trial run is agreed case by case, and we are as flexible on its quantity as production allows.
Once the sample is approved and the deposit received, bulk production usually needs 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.
Shipments go out on FOB, CIF or DDP terms; DDP is available worldwide, and under DDP one all-in price covers delivery to your door, with duties, customs and freight handled by us.
We take a 50% deposit when the order is confirmed, and the remaining 50% is paid before shipment.
A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days.
Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design (its pattern or print, with all colourways); these fees are not refunded or credited against the bulk order.

If you are starting a new label, our starter pack includes three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a catalogue of the ready-made styles we keep in stock and a short guide to launching your own swimwear brand. For your first collection, we also offer separate startup packages that cover design, development and manufacturing. Many new labels use these together with our consulting service.
Courier delivery of samples costs USD 50, paid by the buyer in addition to the sample fee.

A typical order moves from your brief or tech pack to a sample in 10 to 15 days, then to your approval and deposit, 35 to 40 days of bulk production depending on size and season, a full final inspection, and shipment on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.
We quote first: once the price is agreed, we move on to making the sample.
We reply to every enquiry within one business day.
Our buyers include athletic modest swimwear labels, swim schools and clubs, municipal pool programmes, and teams ordering lifeguard and instructor uniforms.

Yes, we also make modest swimwear for retail modest-fashion labels selling in the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Europe, and for wearers who want full sun protection from our UPF 50+ fabric. We adapt lengths, coverage and fit to regional preferences and grade to EU, UK, US or Middle East size charts, or to your own chart.

You can choose from three coverage levels: a tunic reaching mid-thigh, a tunic with an added skirt or cape element, or a knee-length swim dress. The knee-length swim dress is our longest style and is finished with an overlapping or envelope hem.
We make swim hijabs in three constructions: pull-on full-neck, tie-back or adjustable, and a two-piece cap and drape. Sets can also be configured with a hood or with a separate cap.

We finish the face opening of every hood or swim hijab with a soft elastic binding. It holds its shape but does not dig into the face. We also leave a little extra room around the ears for comfort. The neck drape is cut long enough to tuck securely inside the tunic and is finished with a coverstitch hem. A shaped chin panel keeps the chin and neck covered, and an internal drawcord within the wearer's reach lets her adjust the fit herself. Your swim hijab can use a lighter swim knit that breathes better than the tunic fabric. We dye it in the same dye lot as your tunic and leggings, giving one consistent shade across all three pieces, and approve it alongside the tunic and leggings before bulk.

Sleeves come full-length, with or without thumb-loop cuffs, or three-quarter length. For necklines you can pick a small stand collar, a high round neck or a hood joined at the shoulder seam, and leggings come straight, tapered or flared with an elastic or drawcord waistband.

Our standard modest swimwear fabric is 200–210 gsm and rated UPF 50+. It takes up very little water, so your garment stays light when wet, and it dries fast. For sport burkini sets, we add a compression fit and chlorine resistance.

We specify fabric according to where you will wear the garment. For pool use we prioritise chlorine resistance and colourfastness. For open water we prioritise UPF and how the fabric behaves when soaked.

For light shades we recommend a lined front panel. We swim every prototype ourselves, checking drag, shifting and cling as well as opacity when wet, and we check it once more after it dries. Before bulk, we show you that float prevention works on a sample in the water. We also suggest having a swimmer try the fit in the water over a full stroke cycle before you sign off bulk.

To reduce wet cling and hide body contours, we can fully line the tunic or line just the front panel, cut the tunic in a relaxed A-line with 4 to 6 cm of extra ease at the hip, and add a layered skirt or cape over the chest and hips. You can also choose a matt or textured face fabric, a slightly heavier 220 gsm option for the tunic, or darker shades and all-over prints, which show less of the body's outline when wet.

We make swimwear from nylon and polyester swimwear fabrics blended with spandex, such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. On request we source chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, recycled nylon such as ECONYL, recycled polyester such as REPREVE, and Italian Carvico fabrics.

Our UPF 50+ fabrics are tested to AS/NZS 4399, the standard used in Australia and New Zealand, and we supply the UPF test documentation; the standard rating applies to dry, relaxed fabric. Wet and stretched tests, tests on your selected colourway, or tests to EN 13758-1 for the EU or AATCC 183 for the US can be added at an accredited lab, with fees paid by you at cost.

To keep the tunic from floating up, we use elasticated or weighted hems, hem vents, a fitted inner layer and a waist cut close to the body. Tunic hems are split or shaped so the hem won't twist around the swimmer's legs during a stroke.

To keep leggings from riding up, we finish them with a stirrup or a cuff. Leggings sold on their own get a wide, encased waistband that does not roll. We sew in the elastic at the neck, cuffs and ankles under controlled tension, and the cuff and ankle openings get silicone-backed elastic. Drawcords and internal ties sit within the swimmer's reach, and we cut hoods to hold their position without pressing on the throat.
Detachable sleeves and skirts can be fitted with resin snaps or concealed zips, attached at a reinforced point.

Full-coverage one-piece suits can be made as pull-on styles or with a full-length front zip, and we can also place a zip at the centre back or a half zip at the neck, finished with a fabric zip garage at the top. We use corrosion-resistant swim zips that open and close easily when the suit is wet.

Yes, we can build a shelf bra with wire-free, removable contour cups into the tunic or swim dress for light shaping, and add an inner brief or short in matching lining so the wearer needs no separate underlayers.

Yes, we can make a loose tunic that skims the body rather than hugging it, and we control drag through the cut, placing the volume through the shoulders, bust and hips instead of at the hem, without reducing the coverage. A fitted inner layer and an elasticated or weighted hem stop the loose tunic from floating up.

Our classic block, graded S to 3XL, has a 76 cm legging inseam on size M and 4–6 cm of ease at the tunic bust and hip, while our sport block, graded S to 4XL, keeps the same inseam with 0–2 cm of ease for a closer, compression fit. Inseams grade by 1 cm per size across both blocks.

Our kids' modest sets cover ages 3 to 12, graded in five sizes: 3–4, 5–6, 7–8, 9–10 and 11–12 years. Adult swim hijabs come in two graded sizes, S/M and L/XL, and kids' hijabs are graded to the same age sizes as the set.

Yes, we can grade petite and tall versions of your leggings and tunics alongside regular lengths, adjusting legging inseam, tunic length, torso, hem sweep and slit position together so the proportions hold. Curvy fits and grading to your own size chart are also available.
We make custom plus-size collections. Plus-size styles are fully customisable, and we produce curvy fits and larger cup sizes.

A complete two-piece or three-piece modest set sold as one unit counts as one piece toward our minimum of 50 pieces per style in each colour, while tunics, leggings and hijabs sold as separates count separately.

Our burkinis are cut from swim-specific nylon or polyester spandex fabrics, with close-fitting leggings and a fitted inner layer under the tunic, which meets the swim-garment rules most public pools apply. For pools with stricter rules, we can cut the tunic close to the body at mid-thigh length and use chlorine-resistant fabric such as LYCRA Xtra Life, with the fabric composition on the care label for pool staff to check.

Because each piece is cut separately, one retail set can combine a different tunic, legging and hijab size, either made to order as a mixed-size set or packed from separates. We pack mixed-size sets together, with each component labelled.

Yes, we can join the tunic to the leggings with concealed ties, fabric loops or low-profile resin snaps at the inner waist, so the two pieces stay together in the water. You approve where they sit, how firmly they hold and how they feel on the complete sample set before bulk.

On children's sets we use pull-on hijabs with no loose ties, replace hem weights with elasticated hems, and attach sleeves and skirts permanently instead of making them detachable. Every snap, ring, slider and trim on children's styles is sewn or riveted on and passes a 90 N pull test.

sections.heading: Burkini Sets and Matching Pieces Made in China
sections.body:
We make burkinis as two-piece or three-piece sets: a tunic and full-length leggings, paired with either a hood or a separate hijab. We make all the swimwear ourselves in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

To go with your sets, our matching [cover-ups](/cover-up-manufacturer/) include quick-dry swim skirts, swim dresses, long beach kaftans and robes in the same prints and colours. Full-length, long-sleeved options give the same coverage underneath.

sections.heading: Fabrics That Stay Light, Opaque and Sun-Protective in Water

items.title: Nylon-spandex drape
items.text: Our nylon-spandex drapes softly and sits closer to the body when wet, but it holds more water and dries more slowly. On premium lines, you can also choose a matte option with a softer hand.

items.title: Polyester-spandex weight
items.text: Our polyester-spandex holds less water, so it feels lighter after a swim and dries faster. That makes it the right choice for full-length pieces worn all day.

items.title: Full-length fabric comparison
items.text: You compare the two fabrics in full-length samples worn wet. Soaked tunics and leggings show differences in weight, cling and drying time that small dry swatches hide.

items.title: Sampling trade-off
items.text: Comparing both fabrics adds a development round and extra sample cost. For short sport cuts, the performance gap is smaller, so you get less out of that extra work.

items.title: Wet opacity checks
items.text: We keep the garment opaque with a lining or a double layer, then check the finished piece both wet and under stretch.

items.title: Recycled polyamide option
items.text: If you choose recycled polyamide, we offer fabric spun from reclaimed fishing nets and supply its certification with the fabric.

items.title: Fabric sourcing service
items.text: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), we offer 80% nylon 20% spandex blends, matching linings and UPF 50+ options, and on request LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE and Carvico fabrics. We test them for chlorine resistance, colourfastness, stretch, recovery, strength, softness and durability.

sections.heading: Burkini Construction Tested in Motion

items.title: Fastenings in motion
items.text: We keep only the fastenings your design needs. We confirm where each zip, tie and drawcord sits while the wearer moves the way she would in the water.

items.title: Movement over standing
items.text: A standing fitting doesn't show whether fastenings stay comfortable during strokes or bending. Movement shows up rubbing, snagging and fastenings that shift out of reach.

items.title: Fitting time trade-off
items.text: Fitting in motion takes longer. When it shows a pattern problem, another revision comes before approval.

items.title: Seam placement
items.text: We run seams along muscle lines and keep them away from friction points, which cuts down contact in those areas.

items.title: Bust support
items.text: We build in bust support with a compression shelf, and you can specify removable cups as an extra option.

items.title: Protected, reachable closures
items.text: Every zip is chlorine-rated and has a full internal guard behind it. We place drawcords and internal ties where the swimmer can reach them.

items.title: Coverage and matching pieces
items.text: Our [modest swimwear options](/modest-swimwear-manufacturer/) include three coverage levels, three hijab constructions (one is a two-piece cap and drape) and ready-made two-piece or three-piece designs with your branding.

sections.heading: Lead Times and Seasonal Planning

items.title: Start the autumn before
items.text: For a summer season, development starts the autumn before, because chlorine-resistant knits in specific colours get booked up early.

items.title: Book approved colours
items.text: We confirm fabric and colours, then book the knit as soon as the colours are approved. Fabric procurement sets the schedule for chlorine-resistant swimwear, and committing to colours early leaves less room for late trend changes.

items.title: Finish fit details
items.text: We finish the fit details while the fabric is on order. Through our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/), we check testing, documents, sampling and production schedules against your destination market and launch date.

items.title: Confirm order arrangements
items.text: Under our [order terms](/faq/), courier delivery of a sample costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee. We confirm your exact lead time with the order, and independent SGS or BV inspectors are welcome.

items.title: Run bulk production
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive the deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season decide the exact time.

items.title: Inspect before shipment
items.text: Our [quality checks](/about-us/) cover incoming fabric, cutting and sewing. After that come random checks and a full final inspection before shipment.

sections.heading: OEM Burkini Design, Sampling and Water Testing

items.title: Develop your starting point
items.text: Our [Development service](/development/) turns your design, picture or idea into OEM or ODM patterns and fit. We grade XS to 3XL free of charge against US, EU or UK size charts.

items.title: Set the sample timing
items.text: A standard sample takes us 10 to 15 days, so you have a physical garment to assess before bulk production.

items.title: Confirm development fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.title: Swim-test the prototype
items.text: We swim in every prototype to check drag, shifting, cling and wet opacity. Once it's dry, we inspect it again to find any construction or fabric problems.

items.title: Test with your customers
items.text: After our swim tests, you wear-test the revised prototype on your customers' body types and swimming movements, because fit and comfort depend on shape and use.

items.title: Approve after feedback
items.text: We recommend approving the pre-production sample after your customers have wear-tested it.

sections.heading: Price Factors, Minimums and Order Terms
sections.body: Your price comes down to set configuration, bust support and fabric. Once those are settled, we confirm your price.

items.title: Set configuration
items.text: A three-piece set with a separate hijab costs more than a hooded two-piece. It uses more fabric and adds cutting, sewing and packing.

items.title: Support and pricing
items.text: Cups or a compression shelf raise the price, and a simpler two-piece without cups brings it down. We confirm bulk pricing after we've reviewed your design and fabric.

items.title: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We set the minimum there so small and growing labels can order.

items.title: First trial run
items.text: We agree the quantity for your first trial run case by case. How flexible we can be is limited by what production allows.

items.title: Payment terms
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the other 50% before we ship the goods.

items.title: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship FOB, CIF or DDP. With worldwide DDP you get one all-in price for delivery to your door, and we handle freight, customs and duties.

items.title: Quote before sampling
items.text: Our [quote process](/request-a-quote/) prices your order first. Once you agree the price, we start making your sample.

items.title: Contact and response
items.text: [Contact our team](/contact-us/) by email, WhatsApp or the website form. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Can you manufacture burkinis using fabric we supply, and what stretch, recovery and wet-opacity requirements must it meet?
qa.answer: Yes. We manufacture burkinis from your fabric if it has at least 50% stretch in both directions, at least 90% recovery and full opacity when wet and stretched. If it isn't opaque enough, it needs a lining, and lining changes the weight, feel and drying time. We accept fabric by testing a sample first. That adds testing time, and it settles whether you need lining before you supply the full minimum in each colour plus a cutting allowance.

qa.question: Does a complete burkini set count as one piece towards the 50-piece MOQ, and can I order the hijab or leggings separately?
qa.answer: Yes. A complete set of tunic, leggings and hood or hijab counts as one piece towards our minimum of 50 pieces per style in each colour. You can also order hijabs or leggings separately, and each separate piece has its own minimum of 50 pieces per colour.

qa.question: Apart from tunic-and-leggings sets, can you also make one-piece full-body burkinis, sporty athletic burkinis, and swim dresses or skirts?
qa.answer: Yes, we make all of these styles. Our one-piece full-body burkinis are close, streamlined suits that cover both the top and the legs. Sport burkinis pair a shorter fitted tunic with athletic leggings, and swim dresses and swim skirts are worn over leggings.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Which fabrics do you offer that have UPF 50+ sun protection and resist chlorine and salt water?
qa.answer: We offer UPF 50+ fabrics. On request, we also offer chlorine-resistant fabrics such as LYCRA Xtra Life. We test fabrics for chlorine resistance and for colour fastness after repeated chlorine exposure. Our stretch and recovery testing checks that the suit returns to shape after wear and time in the water. We also test strength, softness and durability.

qa.question: Can you grade our styles across an extended size range, including plus sizes and kids' sizes?
qa.answer: Yes. We make styles for women, men and children, and we grade from XS to 3XL against US, EU or UK size charts. We also produce fully customisable plus-size collections with curvy fits and larger cup sizes. We don't charge for grading any size, and we refine the fit as we build each size. You can send us your own size chart, measurement sheet or reference garment, and we cut to it. Once the chart is based on your fit model, we check every production piece against it and set grading rules separately for each style. If you don't have a chart yet, our pattern makers prepare one for your target market. We cover the EU, UK, US, Australia and the Middle East. We also prepare team size charts for club and school programmes. For a new fit, approve the base-size sample on your own fit model in the exact production fabric. That gives us the correct starting point before we fix the grading rules. Swim fabrics differ in stretch and recovery. If you change the fabric, the same pattern fits tighter or looser, and grading from a wrong base carries that error into every size. This approval adds a sampling round and lead time. For repeat styles in a fabric we've already fitted, it matters less.

qa.question: Which ways can you put our logo and artwork on the garments: sublimation, screen print, heat transfer or embroidery?
qa.answer: We apply logos and artwork with sublimation, screen printing, heat transfer or embroidery. We also offer silicone printing and silicone patches. We screen print labels and care instructions using a chlorine-resistant method. We also handle labelling and packaging. That includes branded hang tags, poly bags, retail packaging and printed cartons. For kids' swimwear, we provide branded size labels and packaging.

pages.h1: Rash Guard Manufacturer for Custom and OEM Ranges
pages.hero_lead: In compression or relaxed cuts, we build ranges for surfing, swimming, swim camps and club teams, with long, short or cap sleeves and zip fronts for women's and men's collections.

sections.heading: Rash Guards for Women, Men, Swim Schools and Teams
sections.body:
We make rash guards in compression and relaxed cuts for surfing, swimming, watersports, swim camps and custom team ranges, and you can order collections for women, men, swim schools and clubs.

For women, we offer long sleeves for full UV coverage, short and cap sleeves, zip fronts, fitted or relaxed cuts, and plus sizes that are graded accurately. For men, there are long and short sleeves, compression shirts for training and relaxed styles for surfing, and we add custom branding for your team.

sections.heading: Our Own Rash Guard Factory in Guangzhou, China

items.title: Our own factory
items.text: We make swimwear ourselves in one factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, so your production is never passed to another manufacturer.

items.title: Matching family sets
items.text: We grade one design across kids' and adult sizes and check the print placement on both before bulk production, so the pieces match when they're worn together.

items.title: Children's print placement
items.text: Adult-sized artwork gets cut off or distorted on smaller panels, so we adjust the scale or placement of logos and motifs where needed. Family pieces end up matching rather than identical.

items.title: Resort and hotel ranges
items.text: We also make custom-branded swim rash guards for resort and hotel programmes, with your branding applied across the collection.

items.title: Factory ownership and checks
items.text: With our [factory ownership and quality controls](/about-us/), production and export sit within one company. We check at fabric arrival, cutting and sewing, then carry out random checks and a full final inspection.

items.title: Enquiry response time
items.text: When you [contact our factory](/contact-us/), we reply to every enquiry within one business day, so you know when you'll hear from us.

sections.heading: OEM Rash Guard Orders: Minimums, Samples, Lead Times and Payment
sections.body: We quote factory-direct after reviewing your design and fabric, not from online prices. Under our [pricing and sample-delivery terms](/faq/), samples ship by courier for USD 50 extra.

items.title: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which gives small and growing labels a starting quantity they can reach.

items.title: First trial run
items.text: We agree your first trial quantity case by case. How flexible we can be depends on what production allows.

items.title: Standard samples
items.text: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50. We don't refund this fee or credit it against bulk.

items.title: Design fees
items.text: Each design costs USD 50, which covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. We don't refund this fee or credit it against bulk.

items.title: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

items.title: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.title: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship FOB, CIF or DDP. With worldwide DDP, you get one all-in price delivered to your door, and we handle duties, customs and freight.

items.title: Quote before sampling
items.text: Through our [quote process](/request-a-quote/), we price your order first and only start the sample once you agree to the price.

sections.heading: Rash Guard Fabrics, UPF Ratings and Certifications
sections.body: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), we source 80/20 nylon-spandex with matching linings, and we supply AS/NZS 4399 UPF 50+ documentation; extra lab testing is charged at cost.

items.title: Performance fabric range
items.text: Our four-way-stretch, UV-protective polyester-spandex weighs 180gsm to 320gsm. Water temperature and activity decide the weight first. Board contact and sun exposure decide the fibre.

items.title: Lightweight warm-water fabrics
items.text: At 180 to 200gsm, these fabrics hold little heat and air-dry in about 30 minutes. They suit warm-water surfing, swim lessons and long days in the sun.

items.title: Heavier supportive fabrics
items.text: At 260 to 320gsm, these fabrics keep wearers warmer in cooler water and give firmer compression and muscle support for training and watersports. The trade-off is that they take about 60 minutes to dry.

items.title: Repeated board contact
items.text: For repeated board contact, we recommend tightly knitted 200–240 GSM polyester-spandex or 80/20 nylon-spandex. Nylon stands up to rubbing best, and polyester holds its colour better in sun and salt water.

items.title: Surface wear
items.text: For frequent surfing, we recommend fabrics of 190 GSM or more; mesh and brushed fabrics wear faster against boards and wax.

items.title: Recycled fabric option
items.text: For eco-focused ranges, we offer on request a 190 g/m² fabric made of 78% recycled nylon and 22% spandex. It's rated UPF 50+ and holds GRS and OEKO-TEX certification.

items.title: Training and surf protection
items.text: You can choose moisture-wicking, four-way-stretch, UV-protective blends. We use quick-drying, moisture-wicking fabric for training, and our surf and watersports styles give UPF 50 protection.

items.title: Production certifications
items.text: Our [production certifications](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

sections.heading: Sizes, Sleeve Options, Necklines and Fits You Can Order

items.title: Size range
items.text: Our standard sizing runs from XS to 3XL, and we extend it up to 5XL for your plus-size ranges.

items.title: Sleeves and necklines
items.text: Choose short, long or ¾ sleeves with a crew neck, high neck or quarter-zip neck.

items.title: Compression fit
items.text: Compression fit stays in place and supports muscles during surfing and training. Because it fits tighter, it needs its own size chart or a wear-test.

items.title: Regular fit
items.text: Regular fit puts comfort first for children, swim lessons and resort wear. Back-zip styles make it easier for kids to get dressed and undressed.

items.title: Coverage details
items.text: High necks and cuff thumb loops cover the neck and arms for surfers and swim-school coaches, and the loops keep long sleeves in place.

items.title: Hooded styles
items.text: We make hooded rash guards for extra sun cover in surf and family ranges.

sections.heading: Flatlock and Bonded Seams Built for Board and Water
sections.body:
Every seam gets durable flatlock stitching by default. It works with every fabric we use and comes on every order at standard cost. On compression-fit styles, we place the seams ergonomically.

On orders of 300 pieces or more, you can choose bonded body seams for a cleaner, flatter finish, at a higher cost. Bonding needs a smooth polyester-spandex or nylon-spandex knit at 180–240 GSM. Mesh, brushed thermal, textured fabrics and anything over 240 GSM don't qualify, because the tape can't grip them evenly.

Even on bonded styles, we keep flatlock stitching at the high-stress joins: zip openings, thumb loops, hood joins and underarm gussets.

visuals.caption: Flatlock and bonded seams compared.

sections.heading: Custom Rash Guard Printing, Logos and Names

items.title: Full sublimation printing
items.text: For multi-colour, detailed all-over designs, we print edge to edge in unlimited colours. Sublimation dyes the polyester fibres, so the print doesn't crack or peel and the fabric keeps its stretch.

items.title: Simple logo methods
items.text: Screen printing suits designs with up to three colours. Screen printing or heat transfer puts simple logos onto pre-dyed fabric efficiently, and we help you choose the method.

items.title: Brand colour matching
items.text: We match sublimated rash guards to your exact brand colours and specifications, and we explain the dark-shade limitation before you approve the design.

items.title: Dark shade limitation
items.text: Sublimated black and very dark shades look less deep than fabric dyed in those colours before printing, and that difference stays in the finished garment.

items.title: Individual team personalisation
items.text: We personalise each piece with its own name or number, and we offer full sublimation for your custom team rash guards.

sections.heading: Private Label Rash Guards and Design Customisation

items.title: Private label services
items.text: With our OEM and private label services, you customise the colours, prints, logos, branding and fabric, and add private labels and custom packaging.

items.title: Design starting points
items.text: Our [OEM and ODM development](/development/) starts from your design, picture or idea. Our team either creates the garment or works from your artwork.

items.title: Panels and stitching
items.text: We offer colour-blocked or contrast body panels and contrast flatlock thread. Fix these choices, and any mesh inserts, in your spec sheet before sampling.

items.title: Breathable mesh inserts
items.text: Mesh at the underarms, sides or back makes the garment more breathable but reduces sun coverage in those areas. That makes it right for training and warm-water styles rather than sun-protection ranges.

items.title: Changes after sampling
items.text: Changing panels or inserts alters the pattern, print layout and fabric use, so any change after sampling needs a new sample.

sections.body: If you supply branded trims, our [Swimwear Hardware](/swimwear-hardware/) team checks 2 test pieces of each; send the bulk quantity plus 3% extra at least 7 days before cutting.

items.title: Your supplied fabric
items.text: You can send us your own fabric, or we can import it from your mill once you give us the supplier name and fabric code.

items.title: Fibre and swatch checks
items.text: Before cutting, we check the fibre content against the print method you've chosen and inspect a swatch. Nylon needs digital pigment printing.

items.title: Schedule and quality responsibility
items.text: Supplied or imported fabric adds to the lead time, and if the fabric varies, more of the quality risk sits with you.

items.title: Launch planning service
items.text: With our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/), we confirm the testing, documents, sampling and production schedules for your design and materials, checked against your destination market and launch date.

sections.heading: How Sleeves, Details and Seams Shape Your Quote
sections.body: Long sleeves take more fabric than short or cap sleeves, so they cost more per unit, and thumb loops, zips and extra panels add sewing time. We quote from your spec sheet, fabric and quantity, so list sleeve length, neckline, trims, panels and seam type from the start. A complete specification up front saves repricing later.

sections.heading: Washing and Drying Printed and Bonded Rash Guards
sections.body:
We write the care label for each style around how it's built and decorated, and we add specific warnings for bonded seams. Rinsing, washing gently and drying in the shade protects sublimation, screen prints and heat-transfer logos.

Heat, wringing, bleach and chlorine left in the fabric damage prints, elastane and seam adhesive faster than ordinary wear does. On programme orders, passing these instructions on to whoever does the laundry keeps the garments cared for the same way. Longer instructions need a bigger label. If comfort matters more, we print the care information straight onto the garment instead.

visuals.purpose: Sets out the care steps on our labels in the order the wearer follows them.
visuals.caption: Care steps from our rash guard labels.

items.label: Rinse in fresh water
items.detail: Rinse the rash guard in fresh water after each use.

items.label: Wash cold, inside out
items.detail: Hand wash, or machine wash cold and inside out on a gentle cycle, with no bleach.

items.label: Dry flat in shade
items.detail: Dry flat in the shade, with no tumble drying or ironing. For bonded seams: no water above 30°C, no wringing and no fabric softener.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Can you make thermal or lined rash guards for colder water?
qa.answer: Yes. We make fleece-lined thermal rash guards in brushed polyester-spandex for swimming and surfing in cool water. Fleece-lined fabrics hold warmth, but they breathe less and dry more slowly. We build the construction you choose into a pre-production sample so you can wear-test it before approving bulk.

qa.question: Which fabric options keep white or light-coloured rash guards opaque when wet and stretched?
qa.answer: For opaque coverage, a soft hand and strong stretch, we use a dense 220 GSM fabric of 85% polyester and 15% spandex. You can also add a lining, a double layer or a lined front panel. You judge opacity on the pre-production sample, wet and stretched on a body, not on a flat swatch. Dense fabrics breathe less and dry more slowly, and added layers and sample rounds add cost and lead time.

qa.question: What anti-ride-up options can you make for surf rash guards, such as gripper hems or board-short attachment loops?
qa.answer: On any surf style, we can add a silicone grip hem, a lockdown loop that ties to your board-short drawcord, or both. They keep the shirt down while you paddle and duck-dive. You wear-test your chosen option in the pre-production sample before approving bulk.

qa.question: What zipper backing or chin-guard construction can you provide to prevent rubbing on zip-front rash guards?
qa.answer: We sew a soft 2 cm backing strip along the full length of the zipper and fold a fabric chin guard over the collar zip pull, so the teeth and slider stay off your skin. For extra comfort at the neck, we also offer a soft coil zip with a 3 cm zip garage at the top. You check comfort by wearing the pre-production sample.

qa.question: How do you limit the white base showing through dark sublimation prints when a fitted rash guard stretches?
qa.answer: We print on polyester that's pre-dyed in a matching dark shade, so when it stretches, that colour shows through instead of white. Very light artwork colours can't be printed on this dark base. We also raise ink density by about 15% in the dark areas and check the sample print stretched by 30% before bulk approval. You judge the garment wet and stretched on a body.

A typical order moves from your brief or tech pack to a sample in 10 to 15 days, then to your approval and deposit, 35 to 40 days of bulk production depending on size and season, a full final inspection, and shipment on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.
We take a 50% deposit when the order is confirmed, and the remaining 50% is paid before shipment.
Courier delivery of samples costs USD 50, paid by the buyer in addition to the sample fee.
We quote first: once the price is agreed, we move on to making the sample.
We make our rash guards from polyester-spandex performance blends that weigh 180gsm to 320gsm. These fabrics have four-way stretch and UPF sun protection.
When you place an order, you can choose fabric blends that are moisture-wicking, four-way stretch and UV-protective. For training styles we use fabric that wicks moisture and dries quickly.
Our surf and watersports styles give UPF 50 protection.

For eco-focused ranges, we offer a fabric made of 78% recycled polyester and 22% elastane at 190 g/m². This fabric is rated UPF 50+. We hold GRS certification for it, and it is also OEKO-TEX certified.

Our lighter rash guard fabrics, from 180 to 200gsm, hold little heat and air-dry in about 30 minutes, so they suit warm-water surfing, swim lessons and long days in the sun. Our heavier fabrics, from 260 to 320gsm, keep you warmer in cooler water and give firmer compression and muscle support for training and watersports, but they take about 60 minutes to dry.

For repeated board contact we recommend our tightly knitted 200–240 GSM polyester-spandex or 80/20 nylon-spandex fabrics, as nylon blends resist rubbing best and polyester blends hold their colour better in sun and salt water. Expect light surface fuzzing or pilling on the chest and stomach after about 3 months of frequent surfing, and lighter fabrics under 190 GSM, mesh or brushed fabrics wear faster where they rub on the board and wax.

We make swimwear from nylon and polyester swimwear fabrics blended with spandex, such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. On request we source chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, recycled nylon such as ECONYL, recycled polyester such as REPREVE, and Italian Carvico fabrics.

Our UPF 50+ fabrics are tested to AS/NZS 4399, the standard used in Australia and New Zealand, and we supply the UPF test documentation; the standard rating applies to dry, relaxed fabric. Wet and stretched tests, tests on your selected colourway, or tests to EN 13758-1 for the EU or AATCC 183 for the US can be added at an accredited lab, with fees paid by you at cost.
Our production holds OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.
Our standard sizes run from XS to 3XL, and we extend sizing up to 5XL for plus-size ranges.
You can choose short, long or ¾ sleeves, in a compression fit or a regular fit.

You can order a crew neck, a high neck or a quarter-zip neck, and add thumb loops at the cuffs to keep long sleeves in place. We also make hooded rash guards for extra sun cover in surf and family ranges and back-zip styles that let kids get in and out easily, while high necks and thumb loops suit surfers and swim-school coaches who need full neck and arm coverage.
We use flatlock stitching on every seam of our rash guards, except on orders of 300 pieces or more, where you can choose bonded (glued) seams instead.
On our compression-fit styles, we place the seams ergonomically.

Bonded seams work on smooth polyester-spandex and nylon-spandex knits from 180 to 240 GSM, but not on mesh, brushed thermal or textured fabrics, or on fabrics over 240 GSM where the tape cannot grip evenly. We keep stitched construction at high-stress areas such as zip openings, thumb loops, hood joins and underarm gussets, so a bonded style combines bonded body seams with flatlock stitching at those points.

We offer custom rash guards in two print methods. Full sublimation prints edge to edge in full colour with no limit on colours, so it suits detailed all-over designs. Screen printing suits simpler designs with up to three colours. If you're not sure which method fits your artwork, we'll help you choose.
We match our sublimated rash guards to your exact brand colours and specifications.
We can apply your logo by sublimation, screen printing or heat transfer.
We can personalise each piece with its own name or number. For team rash guards, full sublimation printing is available.
Please note that a sublimated black never looks quite as deep as fabric that was dyed black before printing. We tell you this before you approve your design.
You can customise colours, prints, logos, branding and fabric. We also offer private labels and custom packaging under our OEM and private label services.
Our team can design your rash guard for you, or we can produce it from artwork you send us.

You can choose contrast colours for the flatlock stitching on your rash guards, and we can cut the body into colour-blocked or contrast panels. We also set breathable mesh inserts at the underarms, side panels or back for training and warm-water styles.
Both OEM and ODM work is possible: a new style can start from your own design, a picture or just an idea.

Yes, we accept your own fabric, or we can import it from your mill if you give us the supplier name and fabric code; for sublimation printing it must be polyester, while nylon fabric is printed with digital pigment.
Based on your destination market and launch date, we confirm the testing, documents, sampling and production schedule for your chosen design and materials.

We fit your own branded hardware and trims to your swimwear: send us 2 pieces of each item first so we can check fit and chlorine and salt-water resistance on your sample, then ship the bulk with 3% extra so it reaches our factory at least 7 days before the scheduled cutting date. Our own hardware is supplied as part of garment production and can also be bought on its own at its minimums.

Long sleeves use more fabric than short or cap sleeves, so they cost more per unit, and details such as thumb loops, zips or extra panels add sewing time; bonded seams, available from 300 pieces, cost more than our standard flatlock stitching. We price these choices into the quote for each style based on your spec sheet, fabric and quantity.

We do not list prices online. Each style is priced from your spec sheets, detailed photos or reference images. The quote depends on the style and how complex its construction is, the level of coverage, the fabric and lining, the print method and any custom printing, your labels, branding and packaging, and the quantity you order. We confirm the bulk price after reviewing your design and fabric choice, and you pay factory-direct prices.

Our care labels tell wearers to rinse the rash guard in fresh water after each use, hand wash or machine wash it cold and inside out on a gentle cycle, and dry it flat in the shade with no bleach, tumble drying or ironing, which keeps sublimated prints, screen prints and heat-transfer logos intact. For bonded-seam styles we add a label line warning against water above 30°C, wringing and fabric softener, because heat and twisting weaken the seam tape adhesive.
Yes, for colder water we make fleece-lined thermal rash guards in a brushed polyester-spandex for cool-water swimming and surfing.

For white and light-coloured rash guards we use a dense 220 GSM fabric of 85% polyester and 15% spandex, which gives opaque coverage with a soft hand and strong stretch. We can also add a lining, a double layer or a lined front panel.

For surf rash guards we can add a silicone grip hem and a lockdown loop that ties to the drawcord of your board shorts, so the shirt stays down while you paddle and duck-dive. You can order either option on its own or both together on any surf style.

On zip-front rash guards we sew a soft 2 cm fabric backing strip behind the full length of the zipper and fold a fabric chin guard over the zip pull at the collar, so the teeth and slider never touch your skin. We can also use a soft coil zip with a 3 cm zip garage at the top for extra comfort around the neck.

For dark sublimation designs we can print on a polyester base fabric pre-dyed in a matching dark shade instead of white, so a stretched rash guard shows that colour rather than a white base, though very light colours in the artwork cannot be printed on a dark base. We also raise ink density by about 15% on dark areas and check the print stretched by 30% on your sample before you approve bulk.

pages.h1: Resort Wear Manufacturer for Private Label Collections
pages.hero_lead: From sundresses, maxis and wraps to kaftans, co-ords and palazzo trousers, we produce the pieces your range needs to dress your customers from the pool to dinner.

sections.heading: From Poolside to Evening: Our Full Resort Wear Range
sections.body:
We make resort wear for every part of the holiday day in your range, from poolside cover-ups and beach dresses to smart-casual evening looks. Our dresses include casual sundresses, maxi and midi styles, wraps, skirt sets and evening designs.

To build complete looks, you can add kaftans, sarong sets, co-ords, shirts, printed and embroidered tops, shorts, wide-leg and palazzo trousers, other pants, lightweight woven styles and layering pieces. We make plus size collections too.

sections.heading: Custom Resort Wear Details, Luxury Fabrics and Seam Finishes

items.title: Luxury fabric choices
items.text: If you sell to upscale holiday retail or boutique hotels, we offer linen and silk-blend resort styles as well as embroidered designs.

items.title: Visible seam finishes
items.text: For luxury styles, we specify French seams or bias binding on every visible seam before cutting. This gives loose and sheer garments a finished interior.

items.title: Fray-resistant construction
items.text: Linen and viscose fray with washing and wear. We enclose the edges in French seams or 1 cm self-fabric or cotton bias binding so the seams last longer.

items.title: Covered overlocking
items.text: We use 4-thread overlock only on seams that a lining hides.

items.title: Construction trade-offs
items.text: French seams and binding take longer to sew and cost more than overlocking. Very thick seams and tight curves limit where we can use them, and some of those styles need a lining.

items.title: Sheer fabric coverage
items.text: Under sheer fabrics, we add a full or half lining in cotton voile or viscose, or a separate slip.

items.title: Waist and closure options
items.text: We build waistbands with 3 cm elastic at the back or all the way round, drawcords, concealed side zips or button-and-loop closures.

items.title: Signature detail selection
items.text: Choose a small set of details for each style: a wash, a trim and a construction feature. This gives your collection its identity and keeps costs predictable.

items.title: Trims and fastenings
items.text: We add crochet lace, tassel and fringe edging, smocked bodices and waists, shell or wooden buttons, rope ties and drawcords.

items.title: Prints and washed finishes
items.text: You can choose block, screen or digital prints. Enzyme washes, garment washes and garment dyeing give linen and cotton a softer, lived-in hand.

items.title: Shape and construction
items.text: Tiered skirts, ruffles, pin-tucks, side slits and tie-front closures are construction details you can combine with the trims and finishes you choose.

items.title: Hand-applied decoration
items.text: Our [Embroidery service](/swimwear-embroidery/) decorates bikinis and cover-ups with beads, sequins, stones, rhinestones, beaded chains, sequin appliqués, embroidered patches and crochet trims. The crochet is handmade, and we sew every bead and sequin on individually. We never glue or heat-press them.

sections.heading: Our Own Resort Wear Factory in Guangzhou, China
sections.body:
We make swimwear ourselves in our one factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

Our [factory and company](/about-us/) have been running since 2011. One owner runs both production and export, so we control quality, cost and delivery directly. We check every order all the way through, and if you can't visit, we run audits for you over live video. We take B2B orders only, and you agree each one directly with our team. We aren't an online shop or a third-party marketplace.

sections.heading: Lightweight, Breathable Fabrics Made for Warm Weather
sections.body:
We pick breathable warm-weather fabrics, weights and linings based on whether your garment is worn on its own or over swimwear.

| Fabric or use | Specification and consequence |
|---|---|
| Linen | 100% linen or 55/45 linen-viscose, in 140–190 GSM plain weave. |
| Bamboo | 100% bamboo viscose twill or 95/5 bamboo viscose-spandex jersey, in 120–180 GSM. |
| Organic cotton | 100% organic cotton voile, poplin or gauze, in 70–140 GSM. |
| Viscose | 100% viscose challis, crepe, twill or slub, in 100–150 GSM. |
| Silk blends | 30/70 silk-cotton voile or 20/80 silk-viscose satin, in 70–110 GSM. |
| Opaque standalone garments | For dresses and trousers, we use 170–190 GSM linen, 130–150 GSM viscose twill or crepe, or 120–140 GSM organic cotton poplin. We fully line the body in 70–90 GSM cotton voile or viscose, or half-line skirts and trousers down to the hip. |
| Sheer cover-ups | We use unlined 70–100 GSM cotton voile, gauze, viscose chiffon or silk-cotton voile. If you want a more opaque version, we add a lining. |
| Weight and coverage | Breathable fabrics show through in sunlight. Heavier fabric or a full lining gives more coverage, but the garment is less airy and costs more. Hip-length half-lining doesn't suit every silhouette. |
| Sustainability and sourcing | Our [sustainability provisions](/sustainability/) cover supplier sourcing to suit your design and budget, OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance. |

sections.heading: Private Label Resort Wear With Your Own Prints and Branding

items.title: Your collection route
items.text: You can adapt our ready resort designs with your own prints, details and branding, or develop a complete custom private label collection with us.

items.title: Fabric-specific printing
items.text: We digitally print linen, organic cotton and viscose with pigment or reactive inks. We keep sublimation printing for selected polyester resort fabrics.

items.title: Swim range coordination
items.text: Send us your swimwear artwork or a reference swatch. We match the print and colour on the resort fabric itself so your two ranges go together.

items.title: Print matching costs
items.text: If we match large motifs across seams or coordinated pieces, each garment uses 10% to 20% more fabric and needs extra time for single-layer cutting, so your unit cost goes up. If we match only at the centre front and key seams, you keep most of the visual impact and waste less fabric.

items.title: Engineered placement prints
items.text: With engineered prints, we don't have to match the full repeat on every panel, but you need artwork for each panel and size. The higher setup cost pays off only on large enough orders.

items.title: Matching knit pieces
items.text: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-swimwear-printing/) digitally prints soft polyester knit to match your swimsuit fabrics. We then make it into cover-ups, dresses or short suits.

items.title: Retail-ready brand presentation
items.text: Our [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels service](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/) gives you biodegradable packaging, branded accessories and heat-pressed logos inside the garment. Connected cardboard tags and individual hand-wrapping are optional. We make labels and packaging in-house wherever we can.

items.title: New label support
items.text: Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) gives you three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a catalogue of our stocked styles and a short guide to launching a swimwear brand. We also offer separate design, development and manufacturing startup packages, and new labels combine these with consulting.

sections.heading: Patterns, Size Grading and Fit Approval Before Bulk
sections.body:
We work out your dress proportions from your measurements, a reference garment, a sketch or a full technical specification. Resort dresses and trousers come in XS to 3XL, and our plus size collections come in 1X to 4X.

We fit every style on a size M model and check it against your measurement sheet. For non-stretch wovens, we grade in fixed 5 cm steps at the bust, waist and hip, and we use a separate 6 cm rule for plus sizes. Finished body measurements stay within ±1 cm. Plus sizes get their own grading rather than a stretched version of the core grade, so the proportions still work as body shape changes. The separate plus-size body fit check adds time to sampling.

Our [in-house development team](/development/) handles pattern design, grading and fit development, so you go through fewer rounds of design back-and-forth.

visuals.purpose: Shows the grading steps used at bust, waist and hip for core and plus sizes on non-stretch woven styles.
visuals.caption: Grading steps at bust, waist and hip for non-stretch woven styles

sections.body:
We fit-approve every women's resort style before bulk production. Non-stretch fitted dresses and trousers worn over swimwear get about 6–8 cm of ease at the bust and 8–10 cm at the hip. Relaxed cover-ups get 15–20 cm.

We check this extra room on a model wearing a swimsuit. Then we shape it with darts, side slits, ties or elasticated back waists so the garment doesn't look oversized. A swimsuit adds bulk at the bust and hip, so a cover-up fitted only over bare skin or underwear ends up tight or gaping once it goes over a swimsuit. Stretch fabrics and standalone styles don't get this extra ease. We fit them closer to the body.

visuals.caption: Extra ease for non-stretch styles worn over swimwear

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Can you make men's resort shirts and shorts, or matching family resort pieces, to go with my women's collection?
qa.answer: Yes. We make men's shirts and shorts and kids' pieces alongside your women's styles. We use the same fabric and print so your men's, women's, kids' and swim looks all match. We can also put your logo on our ready-to-brand men's collection.

qa.question: Which choices in a resort style, such as fabric, embroidery, length or lining, raise or lower the unit price?
qa.answer: Silk and linen blends cost more than viscose or cotton, and hand embroidery costs more than machine embroidery. Maxi lengths, full skirts and full linings use more fabric and sewing time. Midi or mini lengths, partial linings and unlined styles cost less. If you take out the lining, that changes the opacity and how we finish the seams. On natural fibres, digital printing suits small runs with many colours, and screen printing costs less per piece on larger runs with fewer colours. If you switch printing methods, your colour options change. We quote fabric, length, lining, embroidery and printing separately so you can compare them.

qa.question: Can the organic cotton and viscose come with recognised certification such as GOTS, OCS or FSC for my sustainability claims?
qa.answer: We buy organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and viscose from mills that use FSC-certified wood pulp, and we send you the mill certificates on request. Our organic cotton styles are GOTS certified. We don't hold OCS or FSC certification ourselves, so finished garments can't carry those labels in our name. You can ask for FSC-certified paper hang tags. Which of our own certificates applies, including OEKO-TEX Standard 100, depends on the fabric you choose.

qa.question: Are any of your ready resort designs in stock for wholesale, or are they all made to order, and can I see a resort catalogue?
qa.answer: We make most resort designs to order, but we keep some styles in stock for wholesale. Ask for our current Resort Wear line sheet to see what's available, and we'll send you the catalogue within 1 to 2 business days.

qa.question: Which of your resort fabrics support machine-washable garments, and which require hand washing, dry cleaning or special drying and ironing instructions?
qa.answer: Our organic cotton, linen and bamboo can go on a gentle 30°C machine cycle. We pre-wash linen, which keeps shrinkage within 3%. Viscose sateen needs a cold hand wash or a delicate cycle, line or flat drying and ironing on low heat. We label silk blends hand wash or dry clean only. We print the care instructions you approve on every care label.

qa.question: Can you manufacture resort garments using fabric and trims that we supply, and what material limitations apply?
qa.answer: Yes. We use your fabric, trims, labels and packaging, or we import fabric from your mill using its supplier name and fabric code. For resort fabrics, all we need is the composition and care data. Sublimation works only on polyester. We inspect your materials when they arrive and tell you about any shortages or defects within 3 business days, before we cut.

If you are starting a new label, our starter pack includes three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a catalogue of the ready-made styles we keep in stock and a short guide to launching your own swimwear brand. For your first collection, we also offer separate startup packages that cover design, development and manufacturing. Many new labels use these together with our consulting service.
Our production team can develop dress proportions from whatever you send us: your measurements, a reference garment, a sketch, or a full technical specification.

We make resort dresses and trousers in sizes XS to 3XL, and our plus size collections run from 1X to 4X. We fit each style on a size M fit model against your measurement sheet, then grade non-stretch woven styles in fixed steps of 5 cm at bust, waist and hip (6 cm for plus sizes), keeping finished body measurements within ±1 cm.
An in-house design team handles pattern design, grading and fit development, which saves you rounds of back-and-forth on the design.
Each women's resort style is fit-approved before we move it into bulk production.

For non-stretch styles worn over swimwear, we add about 6–8 cm of ease at the bust and 8–10 cm at the hip on fitted dresses and trousers, and 15–20 cm on relaxed cover-ups. We shape the extra room with darts, side slits, ties or elasticated back waists, and we check the ease on the fit sample worn over a swimsuit so the garment sits close without looking oversized.

Yes, we make men's resort shirts and shorts and kids' pieces alongside your women's styles, so you can build matching family looks across men's, women's, kids' and swim. We can cut them from the same fabric and print as your women's collection, and our ready-to-brand men's collection can also be labelled with your logo.

Silk and linen blends cost more than viscose or cotton, hand embroidery costs more than machine embroidery, and maxi lengths, full skirts and full linings raise the price because they use more fabric and sewing time, while midi or mini lengths, partial linings and unlined styles bring it down. On natural fibres, digital printing suits small runs with many colours, while screen printing works out cheaper per piece on larger runs with fewer colours, and we quote each option so you can compare.

We source our organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and our viscose from mills that use FSC-certified wood pulp, and send you their mill certificates on request, but we do not hold GOTS, OCS or FSC certification ourselves, so finished garments cannot carry those labels in our name. FSC-certified paper hang tags are available on request, and which of our own certificates, such as OEKO-TEX Standard 100, apply to your order depends on the fabric you choose.

Most of our resort designs are made to order, but we hold some styles in stock for wholesale, so ask us for the current Resort Wear line sheet to see what is available now. We send our catalogue on request, usually within 1 to 2 business days.

Our organic cotton, linen and bamboo resort fabrics suit machine-washable garments on a gentle 30°C cycle, and we can pre-wash linen to keep shrinkage within 3%. Viscose sateen needs a cold hand wash or delicate cycle, line or flat drying and a low-heat iron, while our silk blends are labelled for hand wash or dry clean only, and we print the care instructions you approve on each care label.

Yes, we can make resort garments from your own fabric, trims, labels and packaging, or import fabric from your mill if you give us the supplier name and fabric code. For resort styles we need only the composition and care data for your fabric, sublimation printing works only on polyester fabric, and we inspect your materials on arrival and report any shortages or defects within 3 business days, before cutting.

sections.heading: Our Cover-Up Factory in China for Kaftans, Sarongs and Kimonos
sections.body: We make cover-ups for you to layer over your bikinis and swimsuits, from kaftans, sarongs and kimonos to tunics and beach dresses. We also manufacture swimwear ourselves in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Your range covers maxi and mini lengths and mesh, crochet and printed pieces. Silhouettes can be fitted, oversized, draped, softly structured or asymmetrical, and the style direction can be minimalist, boho, sporty, luxury or high-fashion.

sections.heading: OEM Cover-Up Styles, Silhouettes and Design Details

items.title: Proven or new silhouettes
items.text: If you start from our fitted, wear-tested patterns, you need fewer sample rounds. You can also send us references or a brief for a new design. Our beach cover-up patterns follow resort, cruise and coastal trends.

items.title: Closures and shaping
items.text: Tell us which closures and shaping you want: open fronts, ties, belts, buttons or snaps, drawstring waists and hems, and side or front slits. All of these work on plain or printed fabrics.

items.title: Necklines and sleeves
items.text: Pick V, round, square, off-shoulder or halter necklines, with sleeveless, cap, kimono, bell, puff or long sleeves.

items.title: Functional finishing details
items.text: We add hoods, patch or in-seam pockets, tassel ties and wooden or shell buttons to set your collection apart.

items.title: Sample-led development
items.text: Our [development team](/development/) handles patterns, grading and fit to cut down the back-and-forth. You approve the sample before any bulk order, so you see the quality first.

items.title: Factory and export ownership
items.text: We've operated since 2011 as a [factory-owned production and export company](/about-us/). We control sourcing, dyeing, cutting, sewing, finishing and inspections at each stage. You agree your order directly with our team, not through shops or marketplaces.

items.title: Inspection and sample delivery
items.text: Under our [inspection and sample arrangements](/faq/), you're welcome to have SGS or BV run independent checks before shipment. You pay for courier delivery of samples, which costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

sections.heading: Beach Cover-Up Fabrics, GSM Weights and Coverage
sections.body:
We pick each fabric first for how well it covers when wet and where you'll wear it. Its look and colour come after that.

| Fabric or requirement | What we supply |
|---|---|
| Lightweight selection | We source chiffon, cotton voile, linen, cotton, rayon, rayon challis, bamboo blends, mesh, knit mesh, lace and crochet textiles from around the world. We also supply 100% polyester or any material you specify. For beach and poolside wear, the breathable, skin-gentle options include quick-dry fabrics. |
| Natural-fibre weights | Our cotton voile, linen and rayon fabrics run from 80 to 150 GSM. They come in 100% cotton, 100% linen, linen-cotton blends and 100% viscose, including rayon challis. |
| Blends and mesh | Bamboo viscose comes blended with cotton or spandex. Nylon or polyester knit mesh contains spandex and comes in similar light weights or in heavier constructions for more body. |
| Opaque coverage | Medium-weight linen, cotton, rayon challis and bamboo blends, tighter weaves and knit jersey give coverage without a separate slip. |
| Sheer constructions | Open mesh, crochet, chiffon, cotton voile and lightweight rayon become more see-through when wet. That's why we wear-test every style damp before we grade the full size run. |
| Added coverage | We line pieces fully or at the bodice/body only, using lightweight polyester georgette, cotton voile or soft knit matched to the shell. Heavier fabric, denser weaves and contrasting solid panels also add coverage. |
| Lower-impact options | We offer sustainable and recycled fabrics for your cover-ups. |
| Production credentials | Our [sustainability credentials](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance. |
| Coordinating swimwear | Our [swimwear fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) includes nylon/polyester-spandex fabrics such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. On request, we also supply chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL recycled nylon, REPREVE recycled polyester and Italian Carvico fabrics. |

items.title: Documented sun protection
items.text: For a sun-protection line, we use tested UPF 50+ fabric in closed-weave or knit long-sleeve shirts, tunics and kaftans. The AS/NZS 4399 documentation rates the fabric dry and relaxed.

items.title: UPF claim boundaries
items.text: Sheer, open mesh and crochet pieces are fashion layers, so they carry no UPF claim. On mixed-panel styles, the rating covers only the areas made from tested UPF fabric.

items.title: Shrinkage and creasing
items.text: We pre-shrink cotton, linen and rayon before cutting, which keeps finished shrinkage within 3%. Softening or enzyme washes reduce hard creasing, and linen-rayon or linen-cotton blends wrinkle less.

items.title: Colour and care
items.text: We use dyes and prints rated grade 4 or higher for fastness to light, salt water and washing. Your care instructions say to rinse in fresh water after beach wear and dry in the shade.

items.title: Stretch knit mesh
items.text: Machine-knitted nylon or polyester mesh contains 5–10% spandex and stretches about 30–50%. It springs back to shape and grows very little when wet.

items.title: Hand-crochet growth
items.text: Cotton or rayon crochet has little stretch and lengthens about 5–10% when damp. We pre-wash the yarn and build that drop into the pattern, or we switch to a polyester/nylon blend yarn, which grows less.

items.title: Secure delicate construction
items.text: Chiffon gets French or narrow-overlocked seams, wider allowances and clean hems to stop slippage. On mesh and crochet, we secure yarn ends, bind or tape cut edges and apply an anti-fray finish to stop snagging and unravelling.

items.title: Crochet cost trade-offs
items.text: Dense crochet uses about 1.5 times the yarn of open mesh and takes longer to make. Joined squares, floral medallions and 3D shells add handwork. Open stitches, larger motifs and woven panels bring the cost down.

sections.heading: Swimsuit Cover-Up Sizes, Lengths and Fit
sections.body:
One-size cuts work for loose kaftans and sarongs. Belted, fitted and tailored cover-ups come in graded size runs.

| Fit or measurement | Your options |
|---|---|
| Standard sizing | We offer S-XL, S-L and one size. For your market, we also make plus sizes and custom sizing beyond these runs. |
| One-size coverage | Our one-size kaftans and sarongs fit roughly S to XL (US 4–14) and bust measurements up to 112 cm. Plus-size versions cover 1X to 3X. |
| Sarong dimensions | A standard sarong measures 110 × 170 cm. A short sarong measures 110 × 90 cm. |
| Shoulder-to-hem lengths | Mini is about 80–85 cm, midi 100–110 cm and maxi 130–140 cm. We adjust any of these to your specification. |
| Tailored adjustments | We adjust length, fit and styling on any design, including long and long-sleeve cover-ups in plus sizes. |
| Coordinated collections | Our [matching beachwear service](/couples-matching-swimsuit-manufacturer/) carries your print across women's, men's and kids' lines, including beach shirts, cover-ups and sarongs. Ready-to-brand men's collections are also available. |

sections.heading: Custom Cover-Up Prints, Colours and Trims
sections.body: First we choose the printing method that suits your fabric. Then we adapt the artwork and embellishment to match it.

items.title: Print designs and effects
items.text: We develop leopard, floral and other custom prints for you using digital, screen or sublimation printing, including gradient and ombré effects.

items.title: Soft natural-fibre prints
items.text: On cotton voile, linen and rayon challis, water-based screen or digital inks soak into the fabric, so it keeps its soft hand and fluid drape.

items.title: Sublimation and block limits
items.text: Sublimation needs polyester and doesn't work on those natural fibres. On sheer voile, we keep heavy screen-print blocks small so the fabric doesn't stiffen.

items.title: Decorative finishing options
items.text: We finish your designs with embroidery, lace insertions, metallic accents and beading, and we adapt the embellishment to each fabric.

items.title: Sheer-fabric embroidery limits
items.text: On chiffon, voile and mesh, we keep light, open motifs within about 10 × 10 cm and around 5,000–8,000 stitches. For larger areas we use lace appliqués, so the fabric doesn't pucker or sag.

items.title: Removable embroidery support
items.text: We stitch over a water-soluble or tear-away stabiliser and remove it afterwards, so no stiff backing shows through the sheer fabric.

items.title: Your colour references
items.text: For [custom colour matching](/custom-swimwear-printing/), we work from a picture you send, our own colour chart or your Pantone references.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Which choices make a cover-up cost more, such as maxi length, hand crochet, beading or linen instead of polyester?
qa.answer: Longer maxi and kaftan cuts cost more than simpler polyester styles. So do linings, linen and other natural fibres, and branded or recycled fabrics. If you choose a branded or recycled fabric, we list the price difference as a separate line on your quote. Crochet, beading and embroidery cost more as the handwork gets denser and covers more of the garment. Screen printing adds a setup charge for each colour. To bring the price down without lowering fabric quality, cut back the handwork, shorten the length, or use digital printing for short multicolour runs.

qa.question: Can you cut and sew cover-ups from fabric we supply, including delicate woven and openwork materials?
qa.answer: Yes. We cut and sew the delicate wovens, lace, crochet and other openwork fabrics you send us. For cover-ups, all we need from you is the fabric's composition and care data.

qa.question: How much longer do hand-crochet or hand-beaded cover-ups take to sample and produce than plain or printed styles?
qa.answer: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days. Hand-crochet or hand-beaded samples take about 5 to 7 days more, and embroidered samples take about 2 to 3 days more. In bulk production, hand beading, sequins, rhinestones and hand crochet add 1 to 2 weeks, depending on how dense the work is. Our in-house embroidery adds about 5 to 7 days. We sew every bead and sequin on your cover-ups by hand. None are glued or heat-pressed.

qa.question: Which of your cover-up materials are suitable for wearing into the water rather than only layering over swimwear on shore?
qa.answer: You can wear nylon or polyester-spandex swim fabrics, quick-dry polyester mesh, knit mesh and synthetic-yarn crochet into the water, and they dry fast. If your pieces are for the pool, we can supply chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life on request. Chiffon, cotton voile, linen, rayon and bamboo blends are layers for the shore. Once they're soaked, they get heavy, cling and lose their shape.

qa.question: Can your cotton, linen and rayon cover-up fabrics come with certification such as OEKO-TEX or organic certification?
qa.answer: Yes. Selected cotton, linen and rayon fabrics fall under our OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification for tested fabrics and trims. We buy organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and can send you their certificates on request. Our organic cotton styles are GOTS certified. We don't hold OCS or FSC certification ourselves, so your finished garments can't carry those labels in our name. FSC-certified paper hang tags are available on request.

qa.question: Can you put my swimsuit print on a chiffon or linen cover-up so the set matches, and how close will the colours be?
qa.answer: Yes. We print your swimsuit artwork on chiffon, rayon challis or linen and adjust the colour setup for each fabric. We match both runs to your Pantone references, and you approve strike-offs placed side by side. The same file looks different on swim knit than on a light woven fabric. On sheer or natural-fibre grounds, the print reads slightly softer, which the side-by-side strike-offs show before bulk.

facts.text: We manufacture swimwear ourselves in a single factory of our own in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

Quality is checked at every stage of an order: fabric on arrival, cutting, sewing, then random checks and a full final inspection.

Hand crochet, hand beading and embroidery add labour cost in line with their density and coverage, and screen prints add set-up for each colour, while digital printing suits short runs with many colours.
Yes, we cut and sew cover-ups from your own fabric, including delicate wovens, lace, crochet and other openwork materials, and for cover-ups we need only its composition and care data.

Hand-beading, sequin work, rhinestones and hand crochet add 1 to 2 weeks to your bulk lead time, depending on how dense the work is, and on our cover-ups every bead and sequin is sewn on by hand, never glued or heat-pressed. Samples with hand-crochet or hand-beaded details need about 5 to 7 extra days on top of our standard 10 to 15 days, samples with embroidered details need about 2 to 3 extra days, and embroidery done in our own factory adds about 5 to 7 days to bulk production.

Cover-ups made in our nylon or polyester spandex swim fabrics, quick-dry polyester mesh and knit mesh, or synthetic-yarn crochet can be worn into the water and dry fast, with chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life available on request for pool use. Chiffon, cotton voile, linen, rayon and bamboo blends are made for layering on shore, as they turn heavy, cling and lose shape when soaked.

Our cotton, linen and rayon cover-up fabrics can come under our OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification for tested fabrics and trims, depending on the fabric you choose, and we source organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and send their certificates on request. Yes, we print your swimsuit artwork onto chiffon, rayon challis or linen for a matching cover-up, adjusting the colour setup for each fabric because one file reads differently on swim knit and on a light woven.
