sections.heading: Custom Embroidered Swimwear: Flat, 3D Puff, Appliqué and Patches
sections.body: Flat embroidery keeps your logo edges crisp and your fine text readable on swimwear. For raised detail, we use 3D puff embroidery, which sits slightly above the fabric. Appliqué gives you layered texture: we lay another fabric over the base and stitch it in place. We also make embroidered patches in the size, layout and colours you specify.

sections.heading: Branding from Small Tags to Full Garments, Made in Our Own Factory
sections.body:
We handle your branding at any scale, from small embroidered tags to coverage across the whole garment. We make your swimwear in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. We start with a small logo, and we move to larger coverage once you approve a sample on your actual swim fabric.

Our [ordering FAQ](/faq/) covers how your unit cost falls as quantities rise and how we give custom best-price quotes for 3,000+ pieces, embroidered orders included. It also covers the USD 50 sample courier delivery you pay on top of sample fees, and independent pre-shipment inspection by SGS or BV.

sections.heading: Which Swim Fabrics Take Embroidery Well
sections.body:
Embroidery works reliably on our standard nylon and polyester spandex blends from 180 gsm up, on recycled and chlorine-resistant swim fabrics, and on lined or double-layer areas. We pick the fabric and the placement together and lean towards heavier, stable blends.

We use a stretch stabiliser so the thread moves with the fabric, and we add a soft facing on the side against your skin. Designs go in low-stretch areas such as leg hems or waistbands, because placing them in high-stretch areas causes puckering. On fabrics under 150 gsm and on mesh, ribbed or crinkle textures, we limit designs to outline or light-fill logos no wider than 5 cm. A patch or a lined panel gives you another option. We test-stitch your fabric before sampling.

sections.heading: How We Keep Stitching Flat on Stretch Fabric
sections.body: On stretch nylon or polyester, we prevent puckering by adapting the embroidery setup to knit fabric. We don't just copy a setup made for woven fabric. We back the fabric with a stretch stabiliser, add pull compensation and a light underlay to the stitch file, and test-stitch on your fabric before sampling.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: How do you attach embroidered patches to stretch swim fabric, and can I order the patches by themselves?
qa.answer: We sew patches on around the edge with a zigzag stitch or coverstitch, so the seam stretches with your suit. We don't use heat-seal glue backings because they lift in chlorine and salt water. Yes, you can order patches on their own, starting at 50 pieces per design.

qa.question: What is the smallest lettering, the largest embroidery size and the most thread colours you can stitch in one design on swimwear?
qa.answer: We can stitch lettering as small as 5 mm high with lines at least 1 mm thick. For 3D puff, the minimum is 10 mm high. One hooping fits a design up to 30 x 30 cm, and each design can use up to 12 thread colours.

qa.question: Can you embroider on top of a printed swimsuit fabric or combine embroidery with sequins and appliqué in one design?
qa.answer: Yes. We combine embroidery with sequins, appliqué, printing, laser cutting or embossing. Once your sublimation or digital print is set, we stitch over it and match the thread to your print colours. Beads and sequins go on after the embroidery, away from seams and straps, so they don't rub or snag.

qa.question: What drives the embroidery cost on my order: stitch count, colours, size, technique or number of logo positions?
qa.answer: Stitch count affects cost the most, and fill density drives stitch count more than size does. A solid fill costs more than an outline of the same size. Each logo position needs its own hooping and machine run. Extra colours, 3D puff, appliqué and patches add setup and handling time, and digitising adds a one-off setup charge per design. If you choose outline or open-fill designs with fewer positions and colours, you keep your cost down and the suit stays comfortable.

qa.question: Can you scale the same embroidered logo across children's and adult sizes while keeping its lettering and detail readable?
qa.answer: Yes. We make 2 to 3 size versions, for example about 4 cm wide for children's sizes and 7 cm wide for adult sizes. We redigitise each version instead of shrinking the file, so the lettering stays at least 5 mm high and fine detail stays readable.

qa.question: Can you embroider fabric or pre-cut swimwear panels supplied by us, rather than only your own production or finished garments?
qa.answer: Yes. We embroider fabric or pre-cut swimwear panels that you supply, from 50 pieces per design. 3% spare panels are added to cover setup and machine loss.

qa.question: Which appliqué fabrics do you offer that remain compatible with the base fabric's stretch and wet-use requirements?
qa.answer: We use a stretch swim fabric similar to your base fabric, so both layers stretch and dry together. The options are 80% nylon 20% spandex and polyester spandex, and on request chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, recycled ECONYL nylon and REPREVE polyester. We also offer metallic foil spandex, swim-grade sequin fabric and stretch mesh. We edge them with a stretch satin stitch and back them with a soft facing for wet use.

pages.hero_lead: As a founder or executive, you work with us on positioning, unit economics, sourcing, sales channels and where to put your capital, the decisions that shape your brand.

sections.heading: Swimwear Brand Consulting Built on Execution, Not Theory
sections.body: We work with founders and executives on the business decisions that shape a swimwear brand. Our swimwear consulting covers how you position the business, what each unit earns, how and where you source, which sales channels you sell through and where you put your capital.

sections.heading: What Our Consulting Covers and How It Differs From Design Support
sections.body:
Consulting ends with a written business strategy. Design and development support ends with patterns, fits and samples. Our consulting team handles the business decisions. Our in-house design team handles pattern design, grading, fit development and sampling alongside manufacturing.

Tell us whether you need a business problem solved or a product made. We scope and invoice the two services separately, so you can book either one on its own. Finish the strategy before product work commits you to fabrics and price points.

For new labels, our [Launch Services starter pack and separate startup packages](/swimwear-launch-services/) give you three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a stocked-style catalogue and a short launch guide. You also get separate design, development and manufacturing support for your first collection.

visuals.purpose: Shows the reader how consulting and design support differ in scope and output, so they can choose the one their problem needs.
visuals.caption: Consulting and design support are two separate services with different outputs.

rows.label: What it covers
values: Positioning, unit economics, sourcing strategy, sales channels and capital
Pattern design, grading, fit development and samples

rows.label: Who does the work
values: In-house design team, as hands-on product work

sections.heading: Senior Consultants Backed by Our Own Factory
sections.body:
A senior consultant leads your engagement. They have at least 10 years of experience in swimwear and apparel brands, sourcing and finance, and a research and modelling analyst supports them. You work with them directly, with no agents in between.

Before any cost, fabric or lead-time assumption goes into a deliverable, we check it with our design team and production floor. Those checks use our own factory data. An assumption about another vendor needs that vendor's quote.

We make swimwear in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Because of our [company and factory ownership](/about-us/), production and export sit within one company, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.

sections.heading: Market Sizing, Customer Research and Brand Positioning

items.title: Market size and segments
items.text: We estimate your addressable market and split it into segments. You get customer profiles and an overview of the competitive landscape.

items.title: Target market coverage
items.text: One project covers up to 3 target markets, including the US, EU, UK, Australia or Canada. We size and segment each market separately.

items.title: Local selling windows
items.text: We map swim seasons, roughly March to August in the Northern Hemisphere and September to February in the Southern Hemisphere, along with year-round resort demand. That way your demand estimates and launch timing line up.

items.title: Desk research boundaries
items.text: Our standard research draws on market data, competitor ranges, retail prices and customer reviews. It tells you what competitors sell and what they charge, but not why customers choose them.

items.title: Direct customer research
items.text: When fit or price is uncertain, interviews or surveys test what customers prefer. On request, we add 8 to 12 interviews with target customers or an online survey of around 200 respondents.

items.title: Positioning grounded in gaps
items.text: Once the market and competitor analysis is done, you get a positioning statement, brand architecture and price-value map. The positioning goes after gaps competitors leave open instead of repeating the founder's preferences.

sections.heading: Line Plans, Target Cost Sheets and Vendor Comparisons
sections.body: You get a line plan, target cost sheets and a sourcing strategy, all worked backward from your target landed cost and our minimums.

items.title: Collection depth first
items.text: When something has to give, we cut styles or colourways before we touch fabric or construction quality. A narrower launch gives your customers fewer choices, but it improves sell-through and protects quality.

items.title: Range and launch dates
items.text: We time your drops to each market's season and plan your bikini sets, separates and one-pieces. A first collection uses 8 to 12 styles in 2 to 3 colourways.

items.title: Size range planning
items.text: We set your size range, for example XS to XL, and add cup-sized tops from B to DD where you need them.

items.title: Minimum order quantities
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. A matched bikini set counts as one piece, and separates count individually. We check your choices against your budget.

items.title: Cost option comparisons
items.text: Your target cost sheets compare sublimation with screen printing, and standard with custom-branded hardware and trims. You see the difference in landed cost and unit margin before you commit.

items.title: Vendor assessment criteria
items.text: We compare cost, minimums, lead times, quality and certifications across our factory, other manufacturers, mills and trim suppliers.

items.title: Freedom to source elsewhere
items.text: We judge our own offer on the same criteria. Where another source suits a style better, the comparison shows it, and you're under no obligation to manufacture with us.

items.title: First trial runs
items.text: We agree trial quantities with you case by case, within what production allows.

sections.heading: Ethical Sourcing Standards and Claim Compliance Reviews
sections.body: We set ethical sourcing standards and check your claims before anything is printed. Wording the evidence doesn't support gets dropped, softened or tested, because reprinting after a challenge costs more.

items.title: Market-specific compliance
items.text: We review your claims against up to 3 target markets, such as the US, EU and UK, and build your sustainability story around documented evidence.

items.title: Recycled-content evidence
items.text: We check sustainability and recycled-content claims against our OEKO-TEX Standard 100, GRS, RCS and bluesign certificates, plus the GRS or RCS transaction certificates linked to your order.

items.title: Fabric certificate limits
items.text: A fabric certificate doesn't back every finished-garment claim in every market, so your wording has to match what the documents prove for the goods you ordered.

items.title: Sun protection claims
items.text: We check UPF 50+ claims against AS/NZS 4399 documentation. That standard rates dry, relaxed fabric, not how the fabric performs wet or stretched.

items.title: Garment labelling checks
items.text: Before your labels and hangtags are printed, we review fibre-content and care labels, plus the drawstring and small-part rules for children's swimwear.

items.title: Packaging and extra tests
items.text: We check “recyclable” and “compostable” wording on your packaging. Any additional evidence you need, including wet/stretched UPF results or reports on the styles you ordered, comes from accredited labs, and you pay their fees at cost.

items.title: Fabric sourcing options
items.text: Through our [fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) you get matching linings, blends such as 80% nylon 20% spandex and, on request, LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE and Italian Carvico.

sections.heading: Sales Channels, Online Returns and Wholesale Timing

items.title: Channel strategy outputs
items.text: We plan your mix of direct-to-consumer and wholesale sales. You get a channel strategy, a pricing and promotions framework, and an e-commerce roadmap.

items.title: Online fit and returns
items.text: We build size guides, fit notes and model measurements into your product pages, allow 25 to 35% for returns in your online margins and review return reasons every season. If you leave returns out, your margin looks higher than it really is.

items.title: Wholesale calendar first
items.text: Buyers place orders 6 to 9 months before the selling season. We schedule line sheets, samples and production around those windows so bulk orders arrive before stores need them. If you miss the window, you lose that season.

items.title: Wholesale cash trade-off
items.text: Wholesale ties up cash in production earlier and earns a lower margin per unit than direct sales, so we let its calendar set production dates before we build your online pricing.

sections.body:
Our sales and marketing strategy defines your sales funnel, your target wholesale accounts and the metrics you track. You get a go-to-market plan, a marketing mix, funnel KPIs, target account lists and outreach materials for your team to put to work.

Before handover, name someone on your team to own wholesale outreach. Your team makes the contacts, so buyer relationships stay with your brand and not with an outside adviser.

When it's time to execute, Launch Services produces campaign photography, video, branding and e-commerce content and builds your online store. We then hand it all over for you to own and run. Wholesale sales calls aren't part of Launch Services.

visuals.caption: The strategy gives your team the plan, Launch Services can produce the content, and wholesale relationships stay with you.

values: Go-to-market plan, marketing mix, funnel KPIs, target account lists and outreach materials
Campaign photography, video, branding, e-commerce content and a built online store

rows.label: Who runs it
values: Your own team carries out the plan
Handed over for you to own and run

sections.heading: Financial Models, Margins and Inventory Planning

items.title: Unit economics and capital
items.text: We analyse what each unit earns, build gross margin bridges and assess how quickly you recover your cash. You get a financial model, a margin analysis and a capital-needs plan.

items.title: Pre-launch model inputs
items.text: Before you make your first sale, we work from your target prices, landed-cost estimates based on real fabric and production quotes, and swimwear benchmarks for conversion, returns and acquisition costs.

items.title: Three financial scenarios
items.text: We model conservative, base and upside scenarios that are ready for investor scrutiny. Once you start selling, you swap the benchmark assumptions for your actual results.

items.title: Seasonal size planning
items.text: We size your first buy to the selling window and build its size curve from fit data and category benchmarks, for example S:M:L:XL at 1:2:2:1.

items.title: Restocking proven sellers
items.text: Your first buy stays small and focuses on core sizes. Repeat orders take 35 to 40 days and restock your best sellers, so you don't tie up cash in excess stock upfront.

items.title: End-of-season cash protection
items.text: We build markdowns into your cash forecast. Unsold sizes and colours are the most common reason a young swimwear brand runs short of cash before its second season.

sections.heading: Process Improvement and Team Structure
sections.body:
Before you hire anyone, we map your processes and set out who makes which decisions. Our operations optimisation work gives you a process map, a KPI dashboard and a cost-reduction roadmap, backed by performance management.

Our organisational structure and talent work clarifies roles, assigns decision rights and sets hiring priorities together with you. You get an organisation design, a hiring plan and an analysis of what to build in-house and what to hand to partners. Clear responsibilities and a short KPI list show you where the gaps are, and your first hires fill the roles partners can't cover well.

visuals.caption: Two workstreams, each with its own deliverables.

values: Map your processes and set up performance management
Clarify roles and decision rights, and decide with you which hires come first

rows.label: What you receive
values: Process map, KPI dashboard and cost-reduction roadmap
Organization design, hiring plan and an in-house versus partner analysis

sections.heading: Fixed-Scope Projects and Choosing an Engagement Format

items.title: Fixed-scope launch projects
items.text: Your pre-launch decisions make up a finite project with agreed objectives, deliverables and timeline. We fix the schedule at the start: 6 to 8 weeks from initial consultation to implementation roadmap.

items.title: Single workstream timing
items.text: A focused workstream, such as sourcing strategy, takes 3 to 4 weeks and settles the decision you need without you commissioning a full brand project.

items.title: Weekly working sessions
items.text: Fixed-scope engagements include one 60-minute working session a week over video, and you can attend any session in person at our Guangzhou factory.

items.title: Changes agreed before work
items.text: On every consulting engagement, we agree any scope change with you in writing and quote it before the extra work starts.

items.title: Choosing your format
items.text: If you have a quick question, start with a one-off session. Fixed-scope work settles your launch decisions, and a retainer supports ongoing review once you have live sales and production results.

sections.heading: Advisory Retainers: Sessions, Billing and Notice

items.title: Scheduled advisory time
items.text: If you're scaling your brand, the advisory retainer gives you two 90-minute working sessions a month with senior advice.

items.title: Between-session access
items.text: Between sessions, you can email or message your senior advisor. We reply within one business day to quick checks that unblock your team.

items.title: Focused decision sessions
items.text: Bring a short list of decisions to each session. Detailed pricing, sourcing and range planning belong in focused working time, not in messages.

items.title: Monthly retainer payment
items.text: We invoice consulting separately from production. You pay your retainer at the start of each month by T/T bank transfer in USD or EUR.

items.title: One-off session payment
items.text: You pay for a one-off consulting session in full before it starts, also by T/T bank transfer in USD or EUR.

items.title: Minimum term and notice
items.text: A retainer runs for at least 3 months. After that, either of us can end it with 30 days' written notice.

sections.heading: How Engagements Start: Inputs, Steps and a Roadmap
sections.body: Before we start, send us your target markets, delivery countries, expected quantities, budget and launch date, plus any sales, margin and cost data you have.

items.title: Agree the engagement
items.text: In the initial consultation, we agree the problem, scope and outcomes with you before the work begins.

items.title: Diagnose the business
items.text: We work from your real quantities, costs and margins. If you don't have sales data yet, we work from your brand brief, target prices, competitor benchmarks and our production cost estimates.

items.title: Design the recommendations
items.text: We base every recommendation on costs and order sizes, so it still works once your styles reach sampling and bulk production.

items.title: Decide the implementation
items.text: We tie the outcomes we agreed to implementation decisions and lay out the work in a roadmap your team can carry out.

items.title: Deliver the roadmap
items.text: You get an implementation roadmap with owners, milestones and KPIs, so it's clear who is responsible for what and how progress is measured.

items.title: Continue into execution
items.text: An advisory retainer reviews your progress against the roadmap. For product recommendations, we also offer design, fabric sourcing, production in our factory and delivery.

sections.heading: Samples, Bulk Production, Payment and Shipping Terms

items.title: Standard sample timing
items.text: Working from your brief or tech pack, we have a standard sample ready in 10 to 15 days.

items.title: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. Design costs USD 50 per design, pattern or print, and that covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.title: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season set the exact timing.

items.title: Production payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before it ships.

items.title: Final inspection and shipment
items.text: We carry out a full final inspection, then ship your order on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.

items.title: Worldwide DDP delivery
items.text: DDP is available worldwide. You pay one all-in price for delivery to your door, and we handle duties, customs and freight.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Can I hire you for consulting without placing a production order, including if I keep my existing manufacturer?
qa.answer: Yes. Consulting doesn't require a garment order or any production commitment. You can stay with your existing manufacturer and use us for strategy only.

qa.question: Is this consulting meant for a brand at my stage, from pre-launch to established label?
qa.answer: Yes. We tailor the scope to your stage, whether you're a founder before launch, a label on its first collection, a direct-to-consumer brand moving into wholesale or an established label repositioning.

qa.question: Can I commission only one workstream, such as sourcing strategy or financial planning, rather than a full brand consulting project?
qa.answer: Yes. A single workstream has its own fixed scope, deliverables and timeline, and you can add others later. One workstream takes 3 to 4 weeks.

qa.question: What decides how much a project or retainer will cost me?
qa.answer: Project fees depend on the scope, the number of workstreams, the duration and the deliverables you need, including financial modelling or direct customer research. Retainer fees depend on the number of monthly sessions and the advisory time between them. We confirm your fee in writing before any work starts.

qa.question: Do we own the models and strategy documents you deliver, and can we use them with other suppliers or investors?
qa.answer: Yes. Once you've paid the related fees, the models, reports, strategies, line plans and other files we deliver belong to you, and you can use them with suppliers, partners or investors. We keep copies only to handle your reorders and never use them for other clients.

qa.question: How far before our swimwear collection launch should consulting begin for us to receive and use the recommendations in time?
qa.answer: Start 6 to 9 months before launch. A fixed-scope project delivers its recommendations within 6 to 8 weeks. That leaves time for 10 to 15 days of sampling, 35 to 40 days of bulk production and shipping before the selling season. Settle your line plans and costing before sampling, because late decisions squeeze production time.

qa.question: Will we receive editable financial models, cost sheets and plans that our team can update after the engagement?
qa.answer: Yes. You get models and cost sheets in editable Excel or Google Sheets, with the formulas and assumptions open. Plans and strategy documents come in editable Word, Google Docs or PowerPoint, so your team can keep updating them.

We suggest starting consulting 6 to 9 months before your collection launch. A fixed-scope project typically delivers its recommendations within 6 to 8 weeks, which leaves time for 10 to 15 days of sampling, 35 to 40 days of bulk production and shipping before your selling season begins.

Yes. We hand over financial models and cost sheets as editable Excel or Google Sheets files with all formulas and assumptions left open, and plans and strategy documents as editable Word, Google Docs or PowerPoint files, so your team can update them after the engagement.

pages.title: Swimwear Development: Patterns, Grading & Fit | Strandmill
pages.meta_description: Get swimwear development from patterns to approved samples: graded size ranges, colour and print mockups, and trim sourcing with costing for production.
pages.h1: Swimwear Development from Your Idea to an Approved Sample
pages.hero_lead: You can pick our ready designs with finished patterns and grading, develop custom styles, or mix both, and skip sampling when you change only colours, prints or hardware.

sections.heading: Ready Design, Custom Design or a Mix?
sections.body: You can choose our ready designs, develop custom swimwear, or combine both in one collection. Our ready designs already have finished patterns and grading. If you only change colours or prints, or add your own hardware, you skip sampling and order bulk straight away. If you change the fit or construction, we make a new fit sample first. We manufacture your swimwear ourselves, in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

sections.heading: Quality Checked at Every Stage of Your Order
sections.body: Our [factory ownership and quality controls](/about-us/) keep production and export within one company. That puts quality, cost and delivery under our direct control, and we run checks throughout your order. When you [enquire about development](/contact-us/), we assign you a dedicated swimwear specialist, who arranges a call back to talk through your project.

visuals.purpose: Shows the order of the quality checks that every order goes through, from fabric arrival to final inspection.
visuals.caption: Quality checks at every stage of an order

items.label: Fabric on arrival
items.detail: Incoming fabric is checked when it reaches the factory.

items.label: Cutting
items.detail: Cut pieces are checked at the cutting stage.

items.label: Sewing
items.detail: Garments are checked during sewing.

items.label: Random checks
items.detail: Random checks are made on finished pieces.

items.label: Full final inspection
items.detail: Every order gets a full final inspection.

sections.heading: What You Can Send Us to Start

items.title: Your starting reference
items.text: Send us annotated screenshots, a tech pack, a hand-drawn or digital sketch, or an existing swimsuit or lingerie piece, and we build your custom prototype from it.

items.title: Details beyond drawings
items.text: Development is anchored on your most concrete reference. If you start from a sketch, marked-up photos give us the details a drawing leaves out, including sewing, cleavage, waist and back coverage.

items.title: Accepted file formats
items.text: We take CAD files in DXF (Gerber/AutoCAD) and DGS formats, and tech packs in whatever format you already use.

items.title: Included development work
items.text: The per-design fee covers creating a tech pack from your sketch, along with the CAD pattern or print across all its colourways.

sections.heading: Bust Support and Construction Options
sections.body: We match bust support to your silhouette, your fabric and the support your customers need. We don't add every option available.

items.title: Padding and cups
items.text: You can choose sewn-in or removable padding, moulded cups in sizes A to DD, and foam padding to suit your style.

items.title: Support and construction
items.text: You can choose from underwire channels, removable cup pockets, power mesh, metal back-strap adjusters, invisible seams, high-cut legs and your own branded accessories.

items.title: Fabric choices
items.text: Our [swimwear fabrics](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) include nylon or polyester blended with spandex, such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. When you request them, we also offer chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE or Italian Carvico fabrics.

items.title: Materials before sampling
items.text: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), you can order a USD 80 swatch pack delivered door to door by DHL Express. We credit the full amount against your first bulk purchase order.

sections.heading: Pattern Making, Size Grading and Fit Approval
sections.body: Our in-house team takes care of pattern design, grading and fit development, so there's less back-and-forth over your design.

items.title: Digital pattern drafting
items.text: We draft your patterns to your size chart in 2D AutoCAD, accurate to the millimetre. They're ready 3 to 5 days after we receive your tech pack.

items.title: Fabric-specific ease
items.text: We calculate negative ease for the exact fabric you'll produce in, including how it behaves wet. Then we cut the fabric automatically so sample making stays fast.

items.title: Style assessment
items.text: We review every private label sample for fit, drape, coverage, measurements and appearance. We also control strap tension, leg openings, symmetry and stretch recovery.

items.title: Structured style checks
items.text: On structured styles, our sample review also covers underwires, cup shape and how the hardware is attached.

items.title: Documented fit approval
items.text: We sign off one base size in production fabric against a measurement sheet, not just photos. Your feedback goes into revisions to the pattern and construction.

items.title: Full range confirmation
items.text: Once the fit is approved, we grade the full range and sew and measure the remaining sizes. We confirm the grading of each size before production.

sections.body: Before we start drawing, we talk with you about your target customer, your requirements, the styles you need, your design goals and your brand guidelines. We support both OEM and ODM development, including projects that start with an idea instead of finished technical files. Your tech pack records the measurements, materials, construction and design specifications. The technical flat drawings show seam types, where the elastic goes and the closures.

sections.heading: What the Service Covers and Who Owns the Patterns

items.title: Development through production
items.text: Our service covers pattern making, swimwear product development, size grading, marker making, sampling and bulk production. We work at a scale that keeps smaller launches affordable.

items.title: Development without bulk
items.text: You can book patterns and samples on their own without committing to bulk. If you book both with us, development and production stay together.

items.title: Your custom files
items.text: On fully custom projects, the tech packs and CAD patterns we develop become yours once you've paid the related fees.

items.title: Certified production
items.text: Our [production credentials](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100, GRS, RCS, bluesign, ISO 9001 and WRAP.

sections.heading: Size Ranges and Grading for Every Style
sections.body:
| Sizing option | What we provide |
|---|---|
| Standard grading | We grade from XS to 3XL using internationally recognised body measurements, and we shift sizes up or down to suit your customers. |
| Plus-size grading | Our Plus Size Swimwear range takes grading up to 5XL. |
| Band-and-cup grading | For cup-sized women's swimwear, one-pieces, bikinis and plus-size styles, we work to your chart, including 32B–38DD. Each combination counts as one size. |
| Size breakdown | The breakdown we see most often is 2-S, 4-M, 4-L, 2-XL. |
| Launch size selection | Your core run serves your main customer base. Extended sizes follow once your sales establish demand. |

sections.heading: Colours, Custom Prints and Mockups

items.title: Collection mockups
items.text: We make custom prints in-house. Once you've picked your colours or prints, we prepare mockups for you to approve. If you ask, we also make a free 2D mock-up of your full collection before cutting.

items.title: Physical colour approval
items.text: Before production, we send you sample colour swatches. You sign off colours on physical swatches or a strike-off, not on screen mockups.

items.title: Printed sample timing
items.text: Samples in the actual printed fabric take about one week longer. You can check your print on an A4 strike-off instead.

items.title: Artwork development
items.text: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-swimwear-printing/) takes your artwork as it is, adjusts it or creates it for you, then prepares the production files. New styles and bulk runs go through digital design approval and a physical sample sign-off.

sections.heading: Hardware, Labels and Packaging Alongside Your Samples
sections.body:
With our [Swimwear Hardware service](/swimwear-hardware/), logo or custom-colour hardware samples are ready about 15 to 20 days after you approve the artwork. Standard colour-matched parts take 7 to 10 days. Bulk hardware starts only after you sign off, and we can fit the approved parts onto your garment sample.

Through [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/), we develop and review your labels, hang tags, hygiene liners and packaging at the same time as your garment samples. Your branding is locked before bulk, and making those decisions early takes several weeks off your production schedule.

visuals.caption: Time to a physical hardware sample

sections.heading: Component Sourcing and Production Preparation

items.title: Full or partial sourcing
items.text: We source fabrics, elastic, hardware and tags for you from trusted suppliers. Choosing components takes around 1 week, and longer with some suppliers.

items.title: Choices before costing
items.text: We settle your components before the samples are finished. That way the consumption report and bulk costing match the materials that go into production.

items.title: Bulk component orders
items.text: Before mass production, we report how much of each component your order uses and work out the production cost. Then we help you order the components you need.

items.title: Your supplied materials
items.text: You can send us your own fabric, trims, hardware and labels for sampling. We can also import from your mill if you give us the supplier name and fabric code.

items.title: Sampling fabric quantities
items.text: For sampling, send about 1.5 metres of each fabric and lining for each style in each colour.

items.title: Bulk fabric allowance
items.text: For bulk, send 5% extra fabric. It has to reach our factory at least 7 days before cutting is scheduled.

sections.heading: What Samples Cost and How Approval Works

items.title: Standard sample timing
items.text: Your standard sample is ready for review in 10 to 15 days.

items.title: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design. We don't refund either fee or credit it against your bulk order.

items.title: Sample delivery charge
items.text: [Sample courier delivery](/faq/) costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

items.title: Prototype feedback
items.text: We send you fitting or prototype samples before pre-production approval. You give us feedback, ask for changes and make final adjustments.

items.title: Binding bulk reference
items.text: We schedule bulk only after you approve the pre-production (PP) sample. That sample is the binding reference, and we check production against it.

items.title: Completed order details
items.text: When your goods are ready, we send you a packing list with the quantities and sizes for each style.

items.title: Embroidery timing
items.text: [Embroidery](/swimwear-embroidery/) adds about 2 to 3 days to sampling and 5 to 7 days to bulk. Your quotation confirms the exact timing.

items.title: Returns
items.text: Claims and returns on development and sample orders follow our [terms and conditions](/terms-and-conditions/).

sections.heading: Fit Sampling, Wet Testing and Approval

items.title: Plain first sample
items.text: For a custom design, we get the fit right on a white or black sample first. Then we move on to the colours or prints you've chosen.

items.title: Live model fitting
items.text: A real person wears every fit sample. The base size is M for standard styles and 2XL for plus-size swimwear.

items.title: Dry and wet testing
items.text: We test the same suit on the fit model dry and then wet, checking its stretch, coverage and opacity.

items.title: Correcting wet opacity
items.text: If the fabric goes see-through when wet, we add or replace the lining or switch to a heavier fabric. Then we wet-test it again before we send you your approval sample.

items.title: Revising failed fit
items.text: If you don't approve the fit, we amend the patterns and make new samples after each fitting. Most samples are approved in the first round.

items.title: No-charge corrections
items.text: Minor digital adjustments take minutes and are free. If a sample differs significantly from the approved handover, we remake it at no extra cost.

sections.heading: Starting With Samples Before Bulk
sections.body: Most of our partnerships start with samples, so you can judge our quality for yourself before you place a bulk order. Once you approve a sample and pay the deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

sections.heading: Minimums, Payment and Shipping Terms

items.title: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so ordering stays accessible for small and growing labels.

items.title: First trial run
items.text: We agree your first trial quantities case by case. How flexible we can be is limited by what production allows.

items.title: Payment split
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.title: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship FOB, CIF or DDP. Worldwide DDP gives you one all-in price delivered to your door, and we handle the duties, customs and freight.

sections.heading: Bulk Lead Times and Extra Time for New Moulds or Prints

items.title: Finalise custom development
items.text: You finalise any new mould or custom print before you book bulk, so development time stays separate from production time.

items.title: Allow additional time
items.text: Any style that needs custom development, including a new mould or print, needs an extra 2-3 weeks.

items.title: Meet production prerequisites
items.text: The bulk production lead time starts from your approved sample and our receipt of your deposit.

items.title: Plan bulk production
items.text: Bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Your order size and the season decide where your schedule falls in that range.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: If I send another brand's swimsuit, will you copy it exactly, or do you only use it as a reference for fit and construction?
qa.answer: We use your reference swimsuit for fit, construction and sizing. We don't copy another brand's logos, trademarked prints or protected design details. We measure the reference and turn it into a spec sheet with tolerances, then build the pattern and make the changes you've asked for. Your finished style carries your own branding and artwork.

qa.question: If I launch with ready-to-go styles, could other brands sell the same designs, and how does that compare with the custom route?
qa.answer: Yes. Our ready-to-go designs are non-exclusive and stay available to every buyer, so other brands can sell the same base styles. Your prints, artwork and branding are used only for you, though. Any custom or ODM design we develop for your brand is exclusive to you, and we'll sign an NDA if you ask.

qa.question: What measurement tolerances do you work to when you check samples and graded sizes against my spec sheet?
qa.answer: We check every sample and every graded size against your spec sheet. Straps, bindings and any measurement under 10 cm can be off by no more than 0.5 cm either way (-0.5 to 0.5 cm). Body measurements can be off by no more than 1 cm either way (-1 to 1 cm).

qa.question: Can you show my styles as 3D virtual samples before you sew a physical prototype, or do you only offer 2D mockups?
qa.answer: Yes. Before we sew your first physical prototype, we make 3D virtual samples free of charge, on top of our free 2D collection mockups. You check the proportions, where your artwork's print sits and the colours on screen, so you need fewer rounds of physical samples.

facts.text: We manufacture swimwear ourselves in a single factory of our own in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

You can work from our ready designs, from your own custom designs, or combine both in one collection. Our ready designs already have finished patterns and grading, so if you choose them and only change colours or prints or add your own hardware, you can skip the sampling stage and go directly to a bulk order, but any change to fit or construction needs a new fit sample first.
Production and export sit in one company that owns its factory, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.
When you enquire, we assign a dedicated swimwear specialist to your project, who arranges a call back to talk it through with you.

We can develop a custom design from scratch based on screenshots with your notes, a tech pack, a hand-drawn or digital sketch, or an existing swimsuit or lingerie piece, and build a prototype from it. If you send a sketch, add references showing the sewing details and the cleavage, waist and back coverage you want.
We accept CAD files in DXF (Gerber/AutoCAD) and DGS formats, and you are welcome to send your tech pack in your own format.
Creating the tech pack from your sketch is included in the per-design fee, which also covers the CAD pattern or print we develop for that design in all its colourways.

For bust support we can build in sewn-in or removable padding, molded cups in sizes A to DD, foam padding, underwire channels, removable cup pockets or power mesh, depending on the style. Other construction options include metal adjusters on the back straps, invisible seams and high-cut legs, and you can add your own branded accessories across the range.

We make swimwear from nylon and polyester swimwear fabrics blended with spandex, such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. On request we source chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, recycled nylon such as ECONYL, recycled polyester such as REPREVE, and Italian Carvico fabrics.
An in-house design team handles pattern design, grading and fit development, which saves you rounds of back-and-forth on the design.

Our pattern master drafts your patterns on a digital 2D AutoCAD system to your size chart with millimetre accuracy, so minor changes take only minutes, and the patterns are ready 3 to 5 days after we receive your tech pack. Each pattern includes a fit for you to approve, with negative ease worked out for the exact fabric and the way it behaves wet. Fabric is then cut on an automatic cutting machine, which keeps sample making fast.

Fit is signed off against a measurement sheet rather than photos alone. Each private label style is fit-tested, with strap tension, leg openings, symmetry and stretch recovery all kept under control, and each sample is reviewed for fit, drape, coverage, measurements and appearance; on structured styles we also check the underwires, the cup shape and how the hardware is fixed. Once fit is approved we grade the whole size range, sew and measure the remaining sizes, and confirm the grading in each size before production begins. At every round we revise the patterns and construction according to your feedback.
Both OEM and ODM work is possible: a new style can start from your own design, a picture or just an idea.

Your project begins with a design consultation. You tell us your requirements, design details, style needs, design goals and brand guidelines. If you have no tech pack, our development team creates CAD files from your idea. If you only have sketches, we turn them into tech packs ready for production. We can also prepare technical sketches and specifications for your designs as needed. Each tech pack sets out measurements, materials, construction details and design specifications, and the flat drawings show seam types, elastic placement and closures.

Our development service runs from pattern making and product development through size grading, marker making and sampling to bulk production. We work at a scale that keeps smaller launches affordable and within reach.

Yes, you can book our development service for patterns and samples on its own, with no obligation to place the bulk order with us. On fully custom projects, the tech packs and CAD patterns we develop for you become yours once the related fees are paid.

We size and grade to internationally recognised body measurements, and we can shift sizes up or down to suit your customers. Sizes can be graded from XS to 3XL; the breakdown we see most often is 2-S, 4-M, 4-L, 2-XL.

Our standard development grading runs from XS to 3XL, and for plus-size lines we grade up to 5XL through our Plus Size Swimwear range. On cup-sized women's swimwear, one-pieces, bikinis and plus-size styles, we grade band-and-cup sizes such as 32B–38DD to your chart, and each band-and-cup combination counts as one size.
We produce custom prints in-house, and once you choose a color or print we prepare design mockups for your approval.
On request, we produce a free 2D mock-up of your full collection in your chosen colors and/or prints before cutting.
We provide sample color swatches for your approval before production.
Making samples from actual printed fabric takes about one more week; as an alternative, we can offer an A4 strike-off.

Our designers can take your existing artwork as it is, adjust it, or create a new design, then place it on your styles as mockups and prepare the files for production. You approve a digital mockup of each design, and for new styles and bulk runs we also make a physical sample for you to sign off.

Yes: before bulk we make a physical sample of your logo or custom-colour hardware, such as rings, sliders, clasps and stoppers, ready about 15 to 20 days after you approve the artwork, or 7 to 10 days for standard parts colour-matched to your fabric. We start bulk hardware only after you sign off that sample, and we can fit the approved parts onto your garment sample so you see them in place.

While we make your samples, we can develop your labels and packaging alongside them, including heat-transfer labels, hang tags, hygiene liners and gift bags, and we can make mockups for you to check. We review your prints, labels, hang tags and packaging during sampling and lock them in before bulk production. Settling the branding early can shorten the production schedule by several weeks.
We can source your components, including fabrics, elastic, hardware and tags, fully or partially from trusted suppliers. Component selection takes around 1 week or longer, depending on the supplier.
Before mass production, we report how much of each component your styles consume and calculate the mass production cost, and our team helps you order the components for mass production.

Yes, we accept your own fabric, trims, hardware and labels for sampling, or we can import fabric from your own mill if you give us the supplier name and fabric code. For sampling, send about 1.5 metres of each fabric and lining per style in each colour; for bulk, add 5% extra fabric and make sure it reaches our factory at least 7 days before the scheduled cutting date.
A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days.
Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design (its pattern or print, with all colourways); these fees are not refunded or credited against the bulk order.

We handle sample approvals together with you. First we send fitting or prototype samples so you can give feedback, ask for changes and make final adjustments. Then we send pre-production (PP) samples for your approval. Bulk production is scheduled only after you approve the PP sample, and then your approved style is scaled up to the full order. When the goods are ready, we send you a packing list giving the quantity and sizes for each style.
Courier delivery of samples costs USD 50, paid by the buyer in addition to the sample fee.

You can request fabric swatches from us. If you want to pick materials before sampling, you can order our swatch pack for USD 80, which includes door-to-door DHL Express delivery. We credit the full USD 80 back to you on your first bulk purchase order. The pack holds an actual cut of every swimwear fabric we offer and laser-printed colour cards. It also includes sample metal charms and other accessories, pads in both sewn-in and removable versions, cotton drawstring bags and biodegradable zip-lock bags. Examples of our heat-pressed logos and hygiene stickers are included too. Our fabric design catalogue is shared digitally, as PDF files or photo-sharing links, and we do not print it.

Adding embroidery adds about 2 to 3 days to the sample, including digitising and a stitch-out for your approval, and about 5 to 7 days to bulk production. We confirm the exact time with your quotation, based on the stitch count and the number of pieces.

Before returning anything, you must get a written return authorization number from us, and we will refuse any package or carton that does not show this number. Authorized returns are charged a 20% restocking fee, with return freight billed separately on top of it. We cannot take back goods that have been altered in any way, such as by screen printing, embroidery, relabelling, washing, dyeing or embellishment. Samples cannot be returned.

For custom designs we often make the first fit sample in white or black to lock in the fit. If it is not approved, we revise it: after each fitting we amend the patterns and make new samples. Once the fit is right, we can make samples in your chosen colors or prints. Most of our samples are approved in the first round.
We handle minor adjustments digitally free of charge, and if a sample differs significantly from the approved handover, we remake it at no extra cost.

Every fit sample is tried on a real person, not just a dress form. Our fit model wears the base size, which is M for standard styles and 2XL for plus-size swimwear, and we measure each point against your measurement sheet. We also wear-test the same suit wet to judge its stretch, coverage and opacity. If the piece turns see-through once wet, we add a lining, swap the existing lining or move to a heavier fabric. We then repeat the wet test before the sample comes to you for approval. Only after the base size passes these checks do we grade the remaining sizes.
Most partnerships begin with samples so quality can be judged first, and the bulk order follows once they are approved.
Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, a level set so that small and growing labels can order.
A first trial run is agreed case by case, and we are as flexible on its quantity as production allows.
We take a 50% deposit when the order is confirmed, and the remaining 50% is paid before shipment.
Shipments go out on FOB, CIF or DDP terms; DDP is available worldwide, and under DDP one all-in price covers delivery to your door, with duties, customs and freight handled by us.
Once the sample is approved and the deposit received, bulk production usually needs 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

A typical order moves from your brief or tech pack to a sample in 10 to 15 days, then to your approval and deposit, 35 to 40 days of bulk production depending on size and season, a full final inspection, and shipment on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.
If your style needs custom development, such as a new mould or print, please allow an extra 2-3 weeks.
Quality is checked at every stage of an order: fabric on arrival, cutting, sewing, then random checks and a full final inspection.
Our production holds OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

You can send us an existing swimsuit, and we use it as the reference for fit, construction and sizing, then build the pattern and make any changes you ask for. We follow its fit and construction, but we don't reproduce another brand's logos, trademarked prints or protected design details, so the finished style carries your own branding and artwork.

Our ready-to-go designs stay in our range for all buyers and are not exclusive, so other brands may sell the same base styles, but the prints, artwork and branding you put on them are used only for you. Custom and ODM designs we develop for your brand are exclusive to you, and we sign an NDA on request.
We check every sample and graded size against your spec sheet: finished measurements stay within ±0.5 cm on straps, bindings and any measurement under 10 cm, and within ±1 cm on body measurements.

Yes, we can show your styles as 3D virtual samples before we sew a physical prototype, at no charge, in addition to our free 2D collection mock-ups. This lets you review proportions, print placement and colours on screen and cut down the number of physical sample rounds.

sections.heading: Compostable Corn-Starch Garment Bags and Eco Zip-Lock Bags
sections.body:
Choose your bag by how your customers will dispose of it. Corn-starch garment bags go to industrial composting. Eco zip-lock bags get reused and then go into soft-plastic recycling.

| Detail | Corn-starch garment bags | Eco zip-lock bags |
|---|---|---|
| Composition | No conventional plastic: about 60% corn starch bound with 40% biodegradable PBAT polymer. | Around 70% recyclable LDPE blended with 30% biodegradable cornstarch. |
| Protection | We chose these after trialling biodegradable options. They're free of harmful chemicals and protect your pieces from humidity in storage and on sale. | Waterproof and reusable. |
| Disposal | Biodegrades within about 180 days in industrial composting. It doesn't break down in home compost or landfill. | Goes into soft-plastic recycling, not compost. |
| Standard sizes | 20 x 25 cm for bikini sets and bottoms, 25 x 35 cm for one-pieces and trunks, and 30 x 40 cm for cover-ups and kaftans. | We print your logo below the zip. |
| Film options | Standard 30 µm film, with custom sizes and heavier 50 µm film for padded pieces or retail programmes that require thicker bags. | The material combines recyclable plastic with biodegradable cornstarch. |
| Logo printing | 1 or 2 Pantone-matched spot colours, up to 15 x 15 cm per side, printed on one side or both. | Up to 3 Pantone-matched colours, up to 18 x 20 cm per side, printed on one side or both. |

sections.heading: Tagless Heat Transfer Labels Printed Inside Each Piece

items.title: Comfort against skin
items.text: We heat-press soft labels directly onto the inside of each piece in our factory. This option needs simple, bold artwork, and that applies to both samples and bulk.

items.title: Templates and colours
items.text: You choose our template or your own artwork, a standard or custom shape, and black or white printing.

items.title: Size and legibility
items.text: Finished labels run from 2 x 1 cm to 8 x 6 cm, and every text element must be larger than 5pt.

items.title: Artwork file formats
items.text: Send vector artwork with outlined fonts as AI, EPS or PDF, or a PNG with a transparent background at 300dpi or higher.

items.title: Width and sizing
items.text: Give us your exact print width in centimetres, within the finished-size range, and send your size guide as a separate file.

items.title: Fabric suitability
items.text: Our tests support heat transfers on swimwear and activewear fabrics, except textured swim fabrics such as textured recycled nylon. Those fabrics need a different label option.

items.title: Custom printing artwork
items.text: For [Custom Printing](/custom-swimwear-printing/), send 300 dpi artwork, with scaled, seamless repeats for all-over prints. We adjust repeat, scale and placement to each style.

sections.heading: DTF Logo Transfers for the Outside of the Suit

items.title: Exterior colour branding
items.text: We match DTF logos to your Pantone references and place them on the outside of the suit.

items.title: Flat fabrics only
items.text: Our testing supports DTF on all flat swimwear and activewear fabrics. Textured fabrics need a different branding option.

items.title: Dimensions and sampling
items.text: We produce DTF at any size up to 35 x 10.7 cm (13.8 x 4.2 in), and a DTF sample takes 2-3 days.

items.title: Solid logo limits
items.text: DTF stretches far less than swim fabric, so large solid logos stiffen the area and lift or crack when stretched. For that reason, solid areas on stretch zones are capped at 8 x 8 cm.

items.title: Placement and open designs
items.text: We turn larger artwork into outlines or open designs with gaps of at least 1 mm. We place logos on lower-stretch areas: hips, centre backs or leg hems.

items.title: Thickness and durability
items.text: DTF is about 0.2 to 0.3 mm thick, so it's firmer, less stretchy and longer-lasting. Inside heat transfers are about 0.1 mm thick and softer, and they move with the fabric.

sections.heading: Embroidered Logos for Stretch Swim Fabrics
sections.body: Our [Embroidery service](/swimwear-embroidery/) adds embroidered logos at low-stretch hems or waistbands on swim fabrics from 180 gsm; on lighter or textured fabrics, we use small outline logos or patches.

sections.heading: Hang Tag Shapes, Paper Stocks and Finishes
sections.body: We match the shape and board weight of your hang tag to your brand's look and to the size of the garment.

items.title: Six shape options

items.title: Square dimensions

items.title: Circle and oval

items.title: Paper and finishes
items.text: You can have 350gsm, 400gsm or 600gsm paper board, or 350gsm or 400gsm recycled stock. Each comes in black or white, with a gloss or matte finish.

items.title: Printed brand details

items.title: Branded hardware alternative

sections.heading: Kraft Paper, Plastic and Recycled-Content Hygiene Liners
sections.body:
We choose your hygiene liners based on how long they'll be stored and how humid it is. During sampling, we peel-test the liner you pick on your own lining.

| Detail | Specification and consequence |
|---|---|
| Kraft paper | Comes in 5 shapes. Custom branding needs an order of more than 3,000 units, and you get a free digital mockup. |
| Plastic | Comes in 5 shapes. Custom branding needs an order of more than 3,000 units, and you get a free digital mockup. |
| Recycled content | Made from 90% recycled materials and available in 3 shapes: thong, standard bikini and full coverage. The water-resistant adhesive peels off without residue. Custom branding isn't available. |
| Five shape dimensions | Thong: 12 x 3.5 cm, tapered, for thong and Brazilian cuts. Kids: 9 x 4 cm. Standard bikini: 14 x 5 cm. Full coverage: 16 x 6.5 cm, for high-waist and one-piece styles. Wide: 15 x 7.5 cm, for boy shorts and fuller bottoms. |
| Humid storage | Plastic film doesn't absorb moisture, so it holds more firmly and peels off cleanly in one piece. Kraft holds fine in a normal warehouse, but above about 70% humidity it softens and curls, and after 6 months it tears when removed. If your stock will sit in humid storage for a long time, you need plastic. |
| Adhesive compatibility | The low-tack, pressure-sensitive adhesive holds on our nylon-spandex, polyester-spandex and recycled-nylon linings. It doesn't suit cotton, open mesh or brushed linings. Mesh, crochet, velvet, sequinned or coated surfaces need a sewn-in gusset instead. |
| Storage limits | In normal storage, liners stay put for up to 12 months and come off without marks or damage. Longer storage, or temperatures above 40°C, leaves adhesive behind. |
| Sampling check | Our peel test checks that the liner stays flat through 8 hours of wear and comes off in one piece with no residue, pilling or colour lift. |

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

qa.question: Which packaging options are recyclable, biodegradable or compostable, under what disposal conditions, and do those claims also cover the printed finished packaging?
qa.answer: Our corn-starch bags are biodegradable and break down in industrial composting within about 180 days. They don't break down in home compost or landfill. Our eco zip-lock bags can be recycled anywhere that accepts soft-plastic (LDPE 4) collection. The supplier data covers only the bag material, not your printed finished pack. You check the disposal and warning wording against your market's and your retailer's rules, and we print only wording you've approved in writing.

qa.question: What shelf life and storage conditions should we plan for before biodegradable bags become brittle, sticky or otherwise unsuitable for sale?
qa.answer: Our corn-starch bags stay strong, clear and ready to sell for 12 months from production when they're sealed in cartons below 30°C and out of direct sunlight. Plan to sell through within that window. Long exposure to temperatures above 40°C or to direct sun shortens their life and turns the film brittle or tacky. That's why we produce your bags close to shipment.

qa.question: Can your bags be printed with suffocation warnings and meet FBA or retailer polybag rules?
qa.answer: Yes. We print suffocation warnings on any bag, in the languages you choose, in type of at least 10pt. For Amazon FBA, we use 50 µm (about 2 mil) film that's clear enough for barcode scanning, and we put warnings on every bag with an opening of 12.7 cm (5 in) or wider. For other retailers, we match the thickness, warning text and label placement to the packaging manual you send us.

qa.question: How do you prevent dark or sublimated swimwear fabrics from discolouring a white heat-transfer label?
qa.answer: On dark, bright or sublimated fabrics, we print white labels over an anti-migration blocker and press them at about 130°C so the dye doesn't bleed into the print. Before bulk, we check a pressed strike-off on each fabric. If the dye still shows through, we switch that label to black.

qa.question: My collection uses textured fabric. Which label should I choose instead of a heat transfer or DTF label?
qa.answer: On textured, ribbed or crinkle swim fabrics, we use an embroidered label on a low-stretch waistband or leg hem. The other option is a heat transfer on the smooth inner lining instead of the textured outside. Men's and boys' swim trunks can also take a sewn-on rubber patch.

qa.question: How are hang tags attached without snagging or putting holes in the swimsuit?
qa.answer: We loop cotton or recycled-polyester string, or ribbon, around a strap or through the care label, so the swim fabric is never pierced. If you'd rather have a plastic fastener or safety pin, we attach it only through the sewn-in care label or the seam allowance, never through the body fabric. We use a fine 1 mm needle so it doesn't snag.
